articleTitle: Extension of Two Return Stroke Models to Consider the Influence of Elevated Strike Objects on the Lightning Return Stroke Current and the Radiated Electromagnetic Field: Comparison with Experimental Results
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The presence of an elevated strike object affects markedly both the measured lightning return stroke current and the radiated electromagnetic fields. Recently, the MTL and the TCS lightning return stroke models have been extended to take into account the presence of elevated strike objects. In this paper, we compare theoretical results obtained using these two models with a set of simultaneously recorded data consisting of the current measured at the top of the Peissenberg tower and the associated electric and magnetic fields at about 200 m. It is shown that both the extended MTL and TCS models are able to reproduce with a reasonably good accuracy the magnitude and waveshapes of the electric and magnetic fields. However, the computed field peak derivatives are found to be much higher than the measured values. Possible reasons for this discrepancy are discussed in the paper.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Different Combinations of Metallised Non-Woven Shielding Materials and an Insulating Substrate, for Use as Shielding Envelopes and Small Shielding Boxes
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The characterisation of shielding materials under different measuring conditions is still a difficult topic. In this paper, some measuring methods will be discussed, which allows the characterisation of shielding materials under different conditions. In a first part, the basic concept of both TEM-t and H-t cells will be discussed. The TEM-t cell has been designed for the characterisation for plane wave conditions, and the H-t cells is usable for the magnetic field, near field condition. Concerning the samples to be used, both cells are compatible and easy to use, without any specific preparation of the samples. Due to their design, orientation and field-polarisation depending characteristics can be studied. This property is a big advantage when studying gaskets, joints and other discontinuities in the material. In a second part, the use of these test-methods will be discussed for the characterisation of metallised woven and non-woven materials and their use in applications for small shielding enclosures on PCB- level. Typically, a small box is made in 3D, starting from a flat 2D material. At the edges of the small boxes, a discontinuity can occur in the material. Both cells offer the opportunity to study these problems at a fundamental level. The influence of the type of the supporting (insulating) carrier will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Simple Measurement of the Transfer Impedance of a Connector
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: P. C. T. van der Laan

abstract: A small and inexpensive workbench setup is developed to determine the transfer impedance of shielded connectors. The primary incentive was the need for a fast, simple, accurate, and sensitive method to judge changes in prototypes of small shielded twin lead telecommunication connectors, which are to be combined to large arrays on printed circuit boards. The injected current is directly measured by a sensor integrated in the setup. The induced voltage is determined by a spectrum/network analyzer. The overall sensitivity is 3 μΩ; the frequency range is up to 1 GHz. Calibration does not require special samples. We present the measurements Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> of a special coaxial cable with a small hole in the solid shield which provides a mutual inductance of 0.1 pH. Practical connectors are investigated as well.

articleTitle: A Novel Technique for Damping Screened Room Resonance
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radiated emission measurements in screened rooms suffer from measurement repeatability due to the excitation of room resonances. A possible solution to this problem is by damping the electromagnetic fields in the room through the introduction of small amounts of absorber. The present contribution considers the use of resistive sheets for this purpose. Results from a Finite Difference Time Domain model for an example screened room show that a screened room error in the range of +/- 5 dB to +/- 10 dB may be achieved using minimal layouts of resistive sheets. Experimental measurements on a screened room show a reduction in variations in field levels from +/- 30 dB down to +/- 5 dB.

articleTitle: Coupling Effects on A Multilayer Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: P. C. T. van der Laan

abstract: In a three layer printed circuit board (PCB), a ground plane (GP) acts as return for the current through the tracks; the current distribution in the GP influences the crosstalk between two signal circuits on the PCB, and the generation of common mode current in an external circuit. We placed signal tracks at various positions on the same or on opposite sides of the GP. Analytical and numerical results were obtained; the theory was checked by measurements. EMC design rules for a proper PCB layout and routing can be obtained.

articleTitle: Modelling and Design of a Set-Up for Studies of Transients in Coils
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design of transformers and generators will be more successful and competitive, if the response of the windings to impinged electromagnetic transients can be better understood. This paper presents a set-up where the electromagnetic wave propagation along a coil can be studied. Voltage and current probes with bandwidths of 100 MHz are used. The set-up is modelled by coupled surface current elements and coupled surface charge elements. The skin-depth is considered by means of a Cauer circuit. The simulations are compared to the experimental results.

articleTitle: Lightning Channel's EM Effects on Large Earth Electrodes by Moments Method
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Starting from a previously developed lightning return stroke representation, the electric field propagating into a dissipative soil is considered as incident field for embedded earth electrodes. Then the method of Moments is applied to investigate transient performances of earth electrodes of large size and complex shape. So, primary and secondary currents, field transferred to separate electrodes, electric field on the surface of the soil and voltages arising between different parts of earthed electric equipment can be evaluated. Some application examples are reported.

articleTitle: A Theoretical Model for Thin Shield Effectiveness against ESD Problems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a simple but accurate method for shielding effectiveness computation of thin closed conducting shields on an external ESD current is presented. The spectrum of the ESD current is obtained by means of a simple circuital model and it is after used for the evaluation of the electromagnetic field inside the enclosure. The time history of the excitation current and of the electromotive force induced on a loop placed inside the enclosure is then recovered by an IFFT algorithm. The numerical results obtained with this approach have been validated by measurements.

articleTitle: Optimum Antenna Placement on a Mobile Board with Registration of EMC
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the decisions of optimizing on decrease of antenna coupling coefficients on a mobile board when limitation is to the coverage for each antenna. For the determination of minimum value of antenna coupling coefficient for one pair is used Gauss-Zeidel method of optimizing or the search method. When two or several of antenna pairs have a common antenna then the coordinates of this antenna are determined by compromise. The algorithms of optimum antenna placement have the computer programs and are tested for the case of four antennas.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Coupling to Shielded Cables: Methodology and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coupling of electromagnetic fields inside shielded cables is an important issue in EMC applications, in which the transfer impedance represents one of the main parameters. The paper discusses the last analytical expressions which have been developed for the transfer impedance of braided cables. A general approach for the determination of the internal response of a shielded cable to an external electromagnetic excitation is presented in the frequency domain using the BLT equations. Then, an equivalent time domain form of the BLT equations is presented for the case of a lossless line. An example of calculation of the internal response of a braided cable illuminated by a plane wave in an EMP simulator, using measured and calculated values of the transfer impedance is presented. Calculations are compared with experimental measurements and a reasonable agreement is found.

articleTitle: Research on the System Processing Conductive Interference on Electrified Railway
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric traction has become one of the trends of modem railway, and electromagnetic environment(EME) is consequently interfered along railroads. Contrasting with radiated emission and other disturbances, conductive interference(CI) is relatively the most severe one in regard to signaling control systems[l], especially when microprocessor and electronic devices are being applied. Cl may cause degradation and failure of the equipment, and immunity to Cl, which relates to design of control systems, must be determined as a specification value. Obviously study on Cl has significance to safety and reliability of railway transport. Mathematical modeling of Cl seems too hard, so this paper presents a system on the basis of measuring method. The system featuring advanced chips and techniques can analyze and process Cl. Error combination and test verification show that system meets the designated requirements including precision, EMC and cost.

articleTitle: Effect of Component Choice on the Immunity of Digital Circuits
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio frequency interference (RF.I) can affect the timing of digital circuits by causing jitter in transitions. This effect was compared for six logic families using a novel RF injection circuit. A typical interfering signal (300mV, 30MHz, 80% amplitude modulated at 1kHz) was found to induce jitter varying from 0.52ns (for 74ACT logic) to 7.9ns (for 74ALS logic). The depth of the modulation (but not its frequency) was shown to affect strongly the amount of jitter. The induced jitter was found to increase with the amplitude of the interference, while the frequency response depended on the logic family. The effect of applying RFI to various pins of an integrated circuit was also investigated.

articleTitle: Experience in Preparing Specialists of High Qualification (MSc. and PhD.) in EMC in Mexico (Cinvestav)
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to review the preparation ways of MSc and PhD students in Electromagnetic Compatibility field, mainly in radio communications area, that are carrying out in Research and Advanced Studies Center of Polytechnic Institute of Mexico, this gives the posibility to evaluate the level of successful and assassment.

articleTitle: Optimization of Radioelectronic Means Signals for Providing Electromagnetic Compatibility
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This report suggests algorithms of signal forming using a posteriori estimation of signal-noise medium for radioelectronic complexes. Comparative results of providing EMC efficiency are given under a priori and a posteriori approaches.

articleTitle: Optimization of an Increased Safety Blowing up System
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: There are some electromagnetic disturbances, influencing the reliability and safety of explosive works. First of all, they are: electrostatic charges, arising when attendants or various mechanisms are at work, lightning discharge, high- frequency fields from antennas, sparking of the faulty equipment and fields around the transmission line. A new type of a detonating fuse, carrying out an explosion at the expense of inductive coupling with a loop connecting the wire with the explosive pressfit on is offered. This device provides reliability and safety of work on account of its constructive solutions, raising systems stability to electromagnetic disturbances. The problem of a detonating fuse electrical parameters optimization in terms of the maximum power transfer through a cable from the generator to the initiator of an explosion is investigated. The influence of the generator and the cable electromagnetic characteristics change on the reliability of the system work is estimated.

articleTitle: Some Common Errors in 4-Layer and Multilayer PCB Design
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Designing PCB's under EMC requirements is a very complex job. A lot of design rules should be implemented during the placement of the components and the routing of the PCB traces. Special attention must be given into the routing of both power supply and ground traces on the PCB. In complex systems - and especially when high speed electronics is involved in the design - the use of 4- layer and multilayer PCB's can help to solve some problems dealing with common mode situations. However, the use of 4-layer and multilayer PCB's is not an automatic problem solver and can introduce new problems when not properly applied. In this paper, three common errors are discussed. They are normally occuring when full automatic placement and routing is used with CAD support in PCB design. The three types of errors can be summarised as: swapping of GND and Vcc reference planes within one subsystem, ground noise on I/O lines and perturbation of sensitive analog circuitry due to wrong analog/digital GND partitioning.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Model for the Prediction of Crosstalk in PCB's
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: High integration, high speed and increasing density of electronic circuit, electromagnetic coupling (crosstalk) problems with high degree of uncertainty have been generated, which are difficult to estimate especially in printed circuit boards (PCB's). In this paper, the random geometries of PCB's traces are considered to obtain an efficient probabilistic model for evaluate the crosstalk between microstrip transmission lines. The probabilistic model was developed considering at the same time of the random geometry and an input signal with flat spectral density. The concepts of state variables, cumulant brackets and maximum entropy method were used. A good agreement between theoretical and experimental result for both near and far-end crosstalk was obtained.

articleTitle: The Influence of the Line Parameters on the Coupling to Shielded Multiconductor Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Transmission line theory is used to analyze the disturbing currents on shielded multiconductor transmission lines in dependence on the primary line parameters (parameters per unit length) and the transfer impedance. Therefore, several well-known procedures are used to estimate the primary line parameters of a shielded seven conductor cable. The crosstalk between the inner conductors is simulated and the results are compared to measured values in order to determine the optimum procedure for estimating the primary line parameters. Additionally, different ways are applied to obtain the transfer impedance for the inner conductors of the shielded multiconductor transmission line. All these values are used to calculate the coupling between an outside disturbing shield current and the currents on the inner conductors. The comparison of calculated and measured values for several configurations allows to rate the procedures for determining the transfer impedance for shielded multiconductor transmission lines.

articleTitle: Software Technique to Control EMP in Networks
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes how the random or burst errors due to the potential Electromagnetic pulses (EMP) like lightning electromagnetic pulse (LEMP), nuclear EMP (NEMP), transients, electrical fast transients (EFT), etc., can be controlled by adopting the proposed software technique in the networks.

articleTitle: The Effect of Measurement Environment on the EMI Performance of a Generic ELT
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The TLM algorithm is used to investigate the effect of the test environment on EMC immunity measurements with Equipments Under Test of appreciable size in the frequency range 100 - 150 MHz. The surface currents induced upon the faces of the Equipment Under Test by an incident plane electromagnetic wave are simulated using TLM for the cases of: free space, a perfectly conducting ground plane, a strip line and a Crawford / TEM cell. Comparison of each with the free space case gives insight into measurement deviation from the ideal and provides a metric which is useful in the design of new test cells. It can also be argued that due to reciprocity the environment will also effect the emissions from a device and that the simulations may provide some insight into how significant this effect is. In the final section we report on some initial measurements undertaken to verify the simulations.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Compatibility of High-Voltage Power Systems and Secondary Circuits of Power Substation.
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper discusses the electromagnetic compatibility of high-voltage circuits of power substation and the secondary circuits of this substation. The latter contain the sensitive electronics devices used for antifault control of former power installations. The substation was built on the ground with high specific resistivity. Some disturbances are observed when 150kV busbars were switched. The current in the high voltage circuits of the substation was calculated when the disconnector had switched on and switched off a short line of 150kV and 1000m length with several arc reignitions. The current maximum was more than 300A. The calculated e.m.f. and the disturbance current in cover of secondary circuits was more than 15kV and 10A. The protection devices were considered also. Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of some technical devices (TD) is considered at present as their ability to function satisfactory in the electromagnetic environment with the definite values of levels of the electromagnetic (EM) disturbances without degradation [1], We suppose that in our days it is necessary to extend the conception of EMC in different binary (or triple and more) subjects (influencing on) and objects (exposed to the influence) of technical devices (TD) and of biological creations (BC) or environmental nature (EN) according to scheme of fig. l as subject or object.

articleTitle: The European Pre-Standard ENV 50166 ”Human Exposure to Electromagnetic Fields” in Perspective
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the protection concept of the ENV 50166 for human exposure to electromagnetic fields and compares its limit values with those of other relevant regulations.

articleTitle: Polarity Superposition Method of Signal Detection in Impulsive Noise
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we examine, Non-linear signal processing for impulsive-type noise. In particular, we consider the following namely, Polarity Superposition, Median Filter and M out of N Median Filter, which are simpler to apply than the most likelihood detection method. Subsequently we apply them to a digital communication system that utilizes Phase Shift Keying (PSK) which is subject to an impulsive interference environment.

articleTitle: Characterisation of the Shielding Effectiveness of Equipment Cabinets Containing Apertures
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In an attempt to minimise interference problems between systems, a shield may be used to provide a barrier between a source and any potential receivers. Any metal can be used as an effective shield or enclosure and the theory detailing the shielding effectiveness of such a barrier is relatively straightforward. There are, however, complications in predicting the shielding effectiveness of practical enclosures. Such enclosures will usually have apertures cut in them for cables, displays and ventilation etc. which will obviously degrade and limit the performance of the shield. In this work, guidance is given for predicting the shielding effectiveness of enclosures containing apertures of various shape and size with the investigation covering both experimental and theoretical aspects of the problem.

articleTitle: Finite-Difference Time-Domain Modelling of Small Apertures
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a Finite-Difference Time-Domain (F.D.T.D.) formalism allowing to model small apertures without discretization. This formulation is based on Bethe's small hole theory, which approximate the fields diffracted by a small aperture as equivalent to the fields radiated by an electric and a magnetic dipole. In the model, the analytical fields radiated by these two dipoles are discretized using the classical finite- difference scheme. The model is then validated by comparisons with analytical results or exact F.D.T.D.. Applications and an extension of the model allowing to consider several apertures close to each other will also be presented.

articleTitle: The Management of Pre-Compliance Testing by the GTEM Cell
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the analysis of radiated emission measurements obtained in two different sites: a GTEM cell and a semi anechoic chamber (SAC). Four different correlation algorithms are used. The theoretical evaluation of the radiated electromagnetic field over a ground plane of two elementary radiating element (electric dipole and magnetic loop) is the reference for the results of the two series of test performed with these sources. The statistical analysis was performed on maximum electric field strength data, comparing GTEM calculated levels with SAC measured levels. The effect of the EUT cables has been considered, suggesting a practical for the GTEM measurement procedure.

articleTitle: A Development of the Application of Superminiature Insulating and Neutralizing Devices for Lightning Protection
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Microwave and carrierwave communication and automization equipments are very important ones necessary for transformer stations and electric power plants in the electric power industry. Although they are equiped with dischargers, if when hit by lightning or short circuit of electric lines occurs, the short circuit current would be up to thousands of amperes and the earth voltage up to thousands of voltages too. The equipment damaged from above resons is as often as not. It is forced to equip the communication line and electronic equipments with insulating and neutralizing transformers to prevent them from lightning and strong electric interference, but the old — type insulating and neutralizing transformers application is limited due to the disadvantage of bnlky- ness and lightning damages come often. We have developed the superminiature insulating transformers (SIT) and superminiature neutralizing transformers (SNT) by new technology to overcome the problem, with the effectivness same as or better than the old type ones. This new insulating and neutralizing technology for lightning protection makes electric system to produce a great amount of economic of value.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility Considerations of SS-CDMA and FDM/FM Radio Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the preliminary results of the analysis of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of existing FDM/FM radio systems and the new personal mobile communication systems, sharing the same frequency band, using the direct sequence spread spectrum with code division multiple access techniques (SS-CDMA). The effect of the SS-CDMA system on the FDM/FM radio systems is expressed through the normalised interference noise power at the FDM/FM system output. The result of this analysis is a simple approximation formula for a quick estimation of the interference noise power.

articleTitle: A Test Point Dependent Statistical Method for ESD
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A statistical method for processing data out of ESD tests is presented, which takes into account the dependence of the device response on the point of application of each discharge. As a result, we are able to specify the minimum number of discharges to be applied in any element of a prefixed grid of test points, in such a way as to satisfy a desired confidence level in an assigned confidence interval for the estimated failure rate. The object is reached through a preliminary investigation of the behaviour of the equipment under test, which allows to distribute the lower and the upper limits of the failure rate. Some numerical examples are given, considering the case of failures at different voltage levels, according to the requirements of the IEC 801-2.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Power Supply System and High Frequency Electrotechnological Equipment
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electrical part of high frequency (HF) electrotechnological equipment involves a main nonlinear element - rectifier. Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of a rectifier and a network is well-known when the usual operation modes are used. Some another modes of HF installations performance are less researched, such as operation of power installation connected to not enough powerful network, simultaneous operation of several HF installations etc. An investigation of these problems is a complicated task due to the wish of exact description of the problem and a big volume of necessary calculations and experiments. Time domain and frequency domain analysis have been carried out for the study of EMC problem of power supply system and HF electrotechnological equipment. The changed parameters are short circuit power of a network, short circuit power of a matching transformer, consumer power, etc. Certain modes of HF installation performance were researched, such as couple operation non-linear and linear loads, two different non-linear loads and other. Some recommendations are given for modelling of system HF equipment-power supply network as well as for the use of equipment in the modes which correspond to the national standards.

articleTitle: Lightning Surge Propagation on MV/LV Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A large number of lightning surges on LV distribution networks are transferred to the LV network via the MV/LV distribution transformer. A simulation study has been conducted using ATP for Windows in order to quantify the attenuation of surges through the distribution transformer and to predict surge stresses appearing on LV aerial bundled conductor (abc) circuits. Suitable models have been derived for use in EMTP. The models have been verified by laboratory experiments.

articleTitle: Pecularities of Nonlinear Wave Scattering by the System of a Linear and Nonlinear Scatterers
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present work is devoted to theoretical and experimental investigation of electromagnetic wave scattering by the system of two parallel thin metallic dipoles (or loops) placed in a free space for the case, when only one of them contains nonlinear local load (for example, in the form of a semiconductor diod). We restrict ourselves to the case of a weak nonlinearity. The results of experiments and numerical calculations of the backscattered field at the second harmonic of the transmitted signal as dependent on the distance between scatterers are presented. Opportunities of the using of this study are discussed.

articleTitle: An Isotropic Field Probe using Six Half-Loop Antennas
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper theoretical bases together with the description of the construction of an isotropic broadband probe for near field measurements are shortly presented. The idea of using half loop double-loaded antennas for both electric and magnetic field measurements is investigated with the use of Fourier series expansion method and verified numerically with the method of moments. In order to combine together six independent probes for measurements of six electromagnetic field components, half loop antennas are placed on the metal sphere, which has basically two functions: first it acts as a mirror plate for half-loop antennas, second it is the screen for electronic circuitry of the probe. Very careful investigation of the probe influence on the measured field is carried out. From that analysis it is known that the probe should not be connected to the measurement devices through the standard metal cable. Because of that, to transmit measured signals multi-channel broadband optical link is used. At the end of the paper the prototype of the probe is shortly described.

articleTitle: Prediction of Magnetic Fields Due to Transmission and Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The effective magnetic field strength produced by transmission systems are analysed by evaluating Biot and Savart integral. In the case of overhead lines the field computation take into consideration the disposition of conductors along catenary curves within each span and the effects of adjacent spans are also discussed. The catenary curves are computed according to italian standards when conductor supports are at the same or at different levels; the approximations on the field strength obtained using a second order or a first order representation of conductor curves are discussed. Typical configuration for 380, 220 and 132 kV systems are examined. The magnetic field produced by transmission cables are compared to overhead lines and the cable configuration giving the same maximum effective field strength are evaluated. Finally the magnetic fields produced by lines constituted by distribution cables are considered in the cases of single conductors and of paralleled conductors considering the non uniform current sharing and the possibility to reduce external field.

articleTitle: An Electromagnetic Scattering Model for Studying the Effects of Higher-Order Modes on the Coupling of an Incident Electromagnetic Wave with an Automobile Harness
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper aims to evaluate the effects of an incident electromagnetic wave on an automobile harness and to take into account the effects of higher- order modes. By using a spectral-domain approach, it is possible to evaluate the contribution of each mode in a semi-analytical way. Some simple configurations have been studied for the purpose of testing the method. Solutions are compared with the ones obtained by considering the fundamental mode (i.e., a quasi-TEM mode) only.

articleTitle: Experimental Activity on ESD Effects
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The importance of experimental analysis of the electrostatic discharge (ESD) effects inside an EMC course is highlighted. In particular, a set of tests is presented, useful to experimentally investigate the coupling of the discharge current in structures typically adopted in electronic equipment design: shielded enclosures and cables, and printed circuit boards (PCB) structures. The paper describes the geometry of each structure, together with some obtained results, and shows how the students are asked to formulate a model to predict each coupling mechanism effect, and to evaluate the resulting disturbances from a design point of view.

articleTitle: Analysis of AM-PM Conversion in a Communication Link
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using a new approach of AM-PM conversion introduced by a radiocommunications link is examined, the system is analyzed as a combination of nonlinear and linear blocks connected in cascade. The model is based on Volterra Series and the nonlinear stages are considered as a system with memory which is not feasible with another approaches given in literature. A model for analyzing a system consisting of N blocks connected in cascade is proposed. As an application, different configurations for a radio system are investigated: RF channel in a receptor, in a transmitter and a link including the transmission channel, thus as interfering signals. In this case suitable conditions for minimum AM-PM conversion and either a pre/postdistortion technique as a structure for minimizing are done.

articleTitle: Impact of Radiated Emission Standards on Digital Radio Receiver Performance
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses the impact of Radiated Emission Standards on the performance of Digital Radio Receivers. A simple methodology to derive the Bit Error Probability (BEP) for a digital radio receiver with a colocated unintentional interference source is presented, together with a discussion of the difficulties involved in these kinds of estimations. Special attention is made for so called stealth radio applications, where a low signal to noise ratio is required. A comparison is made between the European Community Euronorm EN55022 for commercial equipment and typical military requirements, MIL- STD-461D. This comparison is motivated by the fact that reduced defence budgets in combination with rapid technological advances in civilian information technology , opens the possibility for an increased use of civilian technology in the armed forces. Previous work [1] has showed the impact of emission standards on radio receiver sensitivity and the ambient noise environment. The discussions in [1] are further developed to a methodology to translate emission requirements into consequences for colocated digital radio systems. As a part of this extension, both the interference and receiver sensitivity threshold levels are assumed to be Gaussian distributed, which should be more close to reality than seeing these levels as fixed. The methodology can be used as a rough tool in the design phase of a system to set relevant emission requirements and to evaluate radiated emission test results from colocated equipment. A closing example is presented where BEP versus separation distance, at a fixed value of Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), is calculated for a Minimum Shift Keying (MSK) radio system, colocated with an undesired source which equals the limits in the standards mentioned above.

articleTitle: EMC Specifications in the Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A survey of existing EMC specifications in the automotive industry is carried out outlining points of convergence and disagreements taking also into account the aims that the EMC specifications try to achieve. There are two major areas of concern; internal EMC and external EMC. Internal EMC is a functional problem; external EMC regards the environment: it is in the interest of human community to avoid electromagnetic pollution.

articleTitle: An Iterative FEM Method for Analyzing Transmission Line Shielding Configurations
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper an iterative FEM method is described for EMC analysis of shielding configurations of multiconductor transmission lines. The shields can exhibit a linear or non-linear magnetic behaviour and an arbitrary shape (closed or open, thin or thick). The analysis involves solution of unbounded non-linear eddy and skin effect problems in terms of the magnetic vector potential. The domain boundlessness is dealt with by introducing a fictitious boundary on which the magnetic vector potential is first guessed and then iteratively updated according to the previous solution. Examples are given showing that the procedure is accurate and rapidly convergent.

articleTitle: Statistical Characterisation of Conducted Emissions on Artemis Power Bus
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The increasing in requested satellite performance during the last few years has produced a correspondent growth in spacecraft primary bus complexity, first of all in terms of number of connected equipments and global power consumption. This growth determines an increasing difficulty in controlling electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) aspects at system level, even if all bus components are fully compliant with EMC specifications at equipment level. A statistical characterisation of Artemis power bus, in terms of conducted emissions, has been carried out within the frame of Artemis program undertaken by Alenia Spazio. The disturbance level evaluated using this approach has then been used to carry out a conducted susceptibility analysis on the power bus itself, in order to verify possible criticities at each equipment input ports.

articleTitle: Modelling of Metal Oxide Varistors for Needs of Simulation of Disturbances in Electrical Supply Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents up-to-date problems of modelling of metal oxide varistors for needs of simulation of performance of electrical supply systems protected with them, during occurrence of different type of disturbances. A trial of electrical parameters determination of selected zinc oxide varistor is presented basing on its voltage-time responses to surge currents. First the residual voltage characteristics were partitioned to resistive and inertial components. This has allowed to determine the values of resistance and electrical inertia of varistor. Dependence of varistor resistance on instantaneous value of surge current and dependence of varistor inertia on average value of current rate-of-rise were also determined. On the base of determined parameters, accurate electrical and digital models of ZnO varistors were proposed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Current Probes in EMC Tests
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Current monitor and current injection probes are examined in view of EMC tests. Particular attention is paid to the Bulk Current Injection Test highlighting some areas of concern with respect to test accuracy and repeatability.

articleTitle: A New System for the Evaluation of Telecom Hardware Robustness
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper shows a methodology for hardware design qualification of telecom apparatus, based on a new tool called THRIS (Telecom Hardware Robustness Inspection System). The increase of printed circuit board complexity and integrated circuits speed makes the hardware robustness more and more critical and difficult to evaluate. The manual fault insertion method so far used for overall system robustness evaluation is no more applicable. The fully automatic procedure for fault insertion implemented in THRIS first uses a post-layout description of the board for a signal integrity analysis to pinpoint possible critical areas, then the same information is used to localize the optimum fault insertion point. The fault actuator is based on a miniaturized electronic jumper that allows practically no impact on system performance during normal operation. EMC issues, as switching noise generated in simulated fault conditions, are taken into account and minimized. Further developments of the tool include the prediction of both radiated and conducted EMC issues related to telecom apparatus.

articleTitle: Simulation of Conductive Interference on Electrified Railway
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes two susceptibility concepts of a track circuit receiver on an electrified rail way.and three methods to measure the antiinterference susceptibility are designed.

articleTitle: Improvement of Protection Circuits for Signal Lines using Special Diodes
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The usual way to realize nonlinear protection circuits is to cascade gas arresters, varistors and suppressor diodes. The scope of this paper is to show alternative ways combining reliable protection with good signal transfer properties, in particular for high frequencies. For this purpose the suitability of Schottky diodes, PIN structures and high bandgap diodesis investigated.

articleTitle: The Influence of Finite Ground Conductivity on Characteristics of a Vertical Mast (Monopole) Antenna with Elevated Feeding
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The unknown current distribution (UCD), input impedance, grounding impedance, and field pattern of a vertical mast antenna, erected over a real ground and having elevated feeding, are presented in this paper. In order to simplify the analysis, the real earthing system is substituted by a small hemispherical electrode at the lower end of the mast, buried in the ground up to earth surface. The elevated feeding of the antenna is approximated by an ideal voltage generator (Dirac delta-generator). The UCD is determined by solving the system of integral equations of two potential (SIE-TP: the Hertz vector potential and electric scalar potential). In this paper the simplified Sommerfeld's expressions are used for both potentials. These simplified expressions are good approximation when the refractive index n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> (earth/air) is much larger than one. The numerical experiments, given in earlier authors' papers, have shown that the all results of computation, obtained for n<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">l0</inf> >3, are in very good agreement with those obtained by rigorous Sommerfeld's formulation.

articleTitle: The Total Bioelectrical Activity of Various Structures of Brain in Condition of Low- Level Microwave Irradiation
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this research was to study the total bioelectrical activity of various brain structures exposed to low-level microwave in pulse and pack- pulse modes. The autors have already paid attention to thr modulation role and spesial sensitivity to microwave of differend brain structures (1-5). Four series of the experiments with thirty he-rabbits weighing 3 Kg have been performed. Series 1 - control with sham-exposure; Series 2 - exposure to microwave (1,5 GHz) in pulse mode at frequency of 0,12Hz; Series 3 - exposure to microwave (1,5 GHz) in pulse mode at frequency of 1000 Hz; Series 4 - exposure to microwave in pack-pulse mode: at a pulse repetition frequency of 1000 Hz, pack-pulse repetition frequency of 0,12 Hz. In all cases of microwave the energy-flux density per pulse was 0,3 mW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. One rabbit was exposedonce to single regime wave for thirty minutes. However each of the animals participated at random in the control series with sham exposure. More detailed quantitative characteristic of experiments and microwave conditions are presented in Tables 1 and 2.

articleTitle: On the Limits and Applicability of the MTL Theory in Predicting Field to Wire Coupling Phenomena
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper aims to investigate accuracy and limits of the model based on the Multiconductor Transmission Line (MTL) theory in predicting fields to wires coupling phenomena. An experimental investigation is carried out in order to discuss the theory validity in different operating conditions. A multiwire line over a ground plane is illuminated by a uniform electromagnetic field considering different angle of incidence, the field frequency and value of the impedance that terminates the multiwire line. The comparison of experimental and theoretical results obtained with a MTL code and a Method Of Moments (MOM) code evidence some phenomena and parameters that affect the validity of the model.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of the EM Coupling between a Loop Antenna and A 3-D Lossy Body Object
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Detail EM modeling of EM coupling effects between a a circular loop antenna and a 3-D lossy body object is presented. The orientation of the loop antenna proximate to the human body is either perpendicular or parallel to the body. The antenna characteristics, such as the input impedance, radiation patterns/polarizations, radiation efficiency (reduced by the body absorption effect), and directive gain and power gain, etc., affected by the human body were numerically computed. Coupled integral equations (CIE) and the method of moments (MoM) are employed to numerically solve this antenna- body coupling problem. The magnetic frill source model is employed for the antenna feed modeling. Numerical examples are presented for the loop antenna of different orientations and positions at 280 MHz.

articleTitle: The Influence of Hardware and Software Structure on the Immunity of Microcontrollers to External Electromagnetic Impulsive Disturbances
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In formerly published papers it was mentioned that the immunity of electronic equipment can depend on the equipment’s internal function. The results of immunity investigations of microcontrollers against impulsive disturbances described in this paper show that the susceptibility depends directly on the microcontroller’s operational functions, especially on the microcommands used for an assembler instruction. Because of this dependence the susceptibility represented by the value of the fault frequency can change within some nanoseconds between 0% and 100%.

articleTitle: Large Scale Measurements of Low Frequency Electromagnetic Fields in Berlin and Field Reducing Activities in Power Stations
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Since Wertheimer/Leeper, USA, published their results of investigations in L979 [1] concerning the correlation of lowfrequency magnetic fields (LMF) and leukaemia in children who lived in the vicinity of overhead lines several epidemiological studies were carried out. The results from measurements taken in Berlin in single detatched family houses were initially assumed as a comparison with measurements taken in large blocks of flats. High dregree of interest also exists concerning exposition values in industry. Difficulties with the electromagnetic field between high power devices and sensible appliances such as electronical instruments and display screens caused the power utility to make efforts to precisely examine every new part of equipment examined prior to its installation in order to minimise its electromagnetic impact. All known technical solutions to minimise LMF are listed and compared. Special attention has been given to the split phase configuration and to the phase transposition. The complete configuration and technical data are given, so that the user can easily follow the procedures and compare the results.

articleTitle: Digital Measurements to Power Filter Design
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A digital procedure for the measurement of conducted electromagnetic interferences (EMI) and the diagnosis of conducted noise emissions is described. It is determined whether the differential or common mode component of conducted noise is dominant. The procedure consists of first digitizing the outputs of the LISN, with a suitable sampling rate, and then obtaining the spectrum of either the differential- and common-mode component on the two conductors by means of a FFT algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coupling Phenomena between a Flat Conductor and a Thick Wall Aperture
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to encounter various Electromagnetic Compatibility problems, a semi-analytical approach is developed to compute the coupling phenomena between a current source and a thick wall aperture. Fields in the region of the thick wall and aperture are expanded in terms of canonical wave solutions. The current distribution on the conductor surfaces is described in terms of superposition of pulse functions. The boundary conditions on the aperture surfaces and on the conductor carrying currents, excited by an external source, are satisfied by using a point-matching technique. In order to reduce the numerical cost, analytical techniques are employed to calculate the matrix of the system. Numerical implementation concepts and preliminary results are discussed.

articleTitle: New High Performance Electromagnetic Compatibility Measurement Facility at INTA
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To fulfill the demand of Electromagnetic Compatibility Tests over aerospace, military and commercial systems and equipment, INTA has built a new Electromagnetic Compatibility Measurement Facility. The facility consists of four shielded chambers and a 24m × 14m × 10m shielded chamber lined with 2.44m of pyramidal absorbers on walls and ceiling. This paper describes this high performance state-of-the-art facility.

articleTitle: Representation of the Effects Caused by Inhomogeneities of Transmission Lines in the TLT
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: As it has been already mentioned in [1] it is possible to take the effects of three-dimensional discontinuities into consideration in the transmission line theory (TLT). To avoid any misunderstandings the line itself is treated as a homogeneous one but at definite points some inhomogeneities cause effects which cannot be handled in the conventional transmission line theory. These discontinuities are the vertical raisers at the two ports of the transmission line and an arbitrary number of bends along the line. The presented theory allow one to take the effects of the inhomogeneities into consideration or to calculate the spectrum of the transmitted energy, the voltage and current at the termination resistance and the curves of the equivalent radiation resistance (see [1] and [2] for more details) respectively. Comparison between measured and according to the presented theory computed results or between these results and the curves of a MOM based procedure respectively show good agreement.

articleTitle: Measurement and Calculation of Propagation Losses in a Concrete Building at 1.5 GHz
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The geometric theory of diffraction (GTD) method was used to calculate the propagation losses in a concrete building at 1.5 GHz. The seven-story building is constructed of reinforced concrete slabs and walls, wooden doors at the front and back of the building, and glass windows on each floor. To simplify calculations and make reasonable assumptions, the other stories of the building, except the first story, were excluded for the simulations. In the simulations, the glass windows, wooden doors, concrete slabs, and concrete walls of the first story of the building were modeled by 66 lossy dielectric plates. The propagation losses obtained by the GTD method were found in the range of 23 to 52 dB. The simulation results of propagation losses were also compared with those obtained from the experimental measurements. It was found that the measurement data made a good agreement with simulation results obtained by the GTD method

articleTitle: FEM Analysis of Low Frequency Magnetic Fields in Metallic Shielded Configurations
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new model to perform a finite element method (FEM) analysis of time-harmonic low- frequency magnetic field in complex shielding configuration is presented. The linear conductive region, i.e. the shield, is eliminated from the FEM domain introducing equivalent conditions, derived by the shielding theory, on the tangential components of the magnetic field on both sides of the shield. The method is efficient since it avoids the FEM discretization of the conductive region and predicts the shielding performances for nonuniform incident magnetic fields taking into account both magnetic field penetration and flux leakage. Illustrative examples are given for two-dimensional shielding configurations.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Zone of Influence of Earth Potential Rise on Telecommunication Installations in Urban Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Paper presents first results in the development of a computer model that may be used for estimation of the zone of influence of earth potential rise on telecommunication installations in urban environment. A procedure is presented that extends the usual computer models for earthing systems in nonuniform to include connected long and numerous uncoated metallic cable shields. Presented results show that theoretical simplified approach is unacceptable since largely underestimate the zone of influence of the earth potential rise.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction of Finite Strip Array due to Chiral Materials
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Plane wave scattering from a finite strip grating on the grounded chiral substrate is analysed in the frequency domain via a decomposition into plane wave spectra by using the method of moments and closed analytical form of the spectral Green's function for the structure under examination. The purpose of this paper is to extend this technique to more complicated structure, that is scattering from a finite array of strips on the grounded chiral layer and to show how chiral materials affect the RCS. Numerical results will be presented for the special case of n strips (n=5).

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Radiation from a Video Output Amplifier inside a Monitor
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method was used to analyze the electromagnetic radiation from a video output amplifier located inside a computer monitor. The multiple grid technique was implemented in the FDTD method to improve the computational efficiency. The video output amplifier was modeled by a rectangular iron container with an equivalent dipole antenna located at the center of one opened wall faced to the cathode-ray-tube (CRT). The coupled electric fields inside and outside the monitor were calculated. It was found that high values of coupled electric fields occurred near the monitor screen. Simulation results of coupled electric fields at a distance of 3 meters from the monitor screen also complied with the FCC regulations.

articleTitle: Distinctive Features of Corona Discharge Induced by the Coupling between Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents first results of a common research project between the High Voltage Laboratory of Power System Faculty of “POLITEHNICA” University of Bucharest and the High Voltage Laboratory of the Polytechnical Faculty of Mons. The subjects of this common research are: • analytical and field study of EM coupling effects on the high frequency behaviour of overhead circuits subject of crossing with HV lines; • distinctive features of the corona discharge located on induced conductors, study in laboratory conditions. The first stage of the project consists in: • analytical evaluation of the additional charge and a first experimental validation; • proposal for a suitable testing arrangement in the laboratory area: electrode specification based on the numerical evaluation of the surface gradient, test performing for adopted measuring systems and the analysis of other components of the test arrangement.

articleTitle: The Use of Experimental Frequency Responses for Transients Calculation in the EMC Nonlinear Problems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The method of numerical calculation of pulse influence on systems, including nonlinear elements and elements with complex dependence of equivalent parameters cm frequency is considered. The method gives the solution of a problem in the time domain.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility in Railway Systems: Standard and Application
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article describes the principle EMC standards applied to the railway sector, with particular reference to the set of new standards ENV 50121. At experimental level, these standards must be validated with the contribution of railway operators and manufacturers. The experience gained in this process has provided interesting results regarding improved awareness of EMC problems with a view to producing a consistent regulatory framework.

articleTitle: Geomagnetic Variations Caused by Camouflet Explosions: Theoretical Model and Experimental Data Analysis
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the paper the geomagnetic variation generation by camouflet underground nuclear explosions considered. Two stages of explosion are investigated. At initial stage the main mechanism GMV excitation is assumed to be Earth magnetic field expulsion by hot plasma ball and occurrence time-varying magnetic dipole moment. At last stage, when Earth magnetic field has penetrated inside the plasma ball, standing sound wave in cavity creates oscillating magnetic moment, resulting in GMV fluctuations following main pulse. The electrical currents of explosion origin diffusion in conductive ground discussed. For each explosion stage the GMV electric field intensity is calculated. The results are compared with Nevada 1958 records. New specific method for records processing is developed. The calculated signal shape is in a good agreement with typical record. Computed vibrations «period» following the main signal pulse depends on TNT equivalent, explosion depth and surrounding medium density. Experimental records support the dependence.

articleTitle: Coupling of Short Circuit Power System to Underground Multiconductor Cables using ETLEs
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper addresses a novel method to calculate the coupling of short circuit currents of power system to two parallel underground conductors using the equivalent transmission line equations (ETLEs). Earth conduction effect, earth surface boundary, and mutual coupling between the two conductors, as well as impressed fields from the power system are all accounted for simultaneously in the analysis. A typical example is discussed and the computational results are compared with experimental results.

articleTitle: Overvoltages Induced by Lightning on Overhead Power and Distribution Lines with SAG
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Researchers working on the problem of the coupling of lightning electromagnetic fields to overhead lines have suggested that, if the formulation of the coupling problem given by Agrawal et al. is adopted, only the horizontal component of the electric field drives current in the direction of the line and that the vertical component induces current only at the vertical terminations. All of these studies assume that the wires are perfectly horizontal. In practice, however, the wires exhibit sag. A theoretical study of the effect of the sag in overhead conductors has been recently presented by Rubinstein but no experimental validation is available in the literature. In this paper, we report on the experimental test of the theory presented by Rubinstein. To carry out the test, an EMP (Electromagnetic Pulse) simulator and a model line were used. Measured and calculated waveforms are in reasonable agreement in amplitude and in wave shape, although the wave shape agreement worsens for larger amounts of sag. It is shown that the curvature of the wires results in a reduction of lightning-induced voltage magnitudes. Therefore, one can treat the perfectly horizontal wire case as a worst case.

articleTitle: Low-Level-EMC-Test-System
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Non destructive EMC testing of devices and components is of gaining importance. This paper shows the realization of a comfortable and modestly instrumented measuring system. It explains the possibility to calculate response signals for arbitrary linear systems (DUT: device under test) as well as for arbitrary excitation pulses including the required determination of the transfer function of the DUT and of the sensors used for the measurements. The restrictions that are imposed on the DUT, the measuring system and the various kinds of pulses are discussed. The practical limitations due to the measuring system and the occurring effects as well as possible techniques to cope with these limitations will be shown by a case study.

articleTitle: Development of EMC Course
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Undergraduate electrical engineer's education in The Marine Technical University includes EMC course since 1987. The university prepares specialists for shipbuilding industry. The students of different specialities study EMC course for 51 - 85 hours. Lectures, up to 10 laboratory experiments and individual course work are in the schedule of study. Computer simulation of noise generation and propagation were used for EMC training for more than 5 years. Now new multimedia software for EMC education is under development. IBM compatible PC with sound blaster, video blaster and CD ROM is used for education. The first step was slide presentation of EMP testing with sound and explanation. The next step was development of animation and video to give an information about test simulators and procedures of testing. Last step is interactive multimedia training software.

articleTitle: Mathematical Simulation of a Gas Discharge Protector using ATP-EMTP
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The issue of protection and protection coordination is of increasing importance due to the vulnerability of electronic equipment to voltage surges and transients. In order to properly co-ordinate the different protection units of a protection system, all the different parts must be considered in the design process. This paper presents an ATP-EMTP model for the gas discharge protector in which all the different discharge phases are considered. Further, the model has been proven to be useful in hybrid circuit simulations.

articleTitle: Importance of Losses in the Determination of Lightning-Induced Voltages on Overhead Lines
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the determination of lightning-induced voltages on overhead lines, ground losses play a role in both the evaluation of the lightning radiated electromagnetic fields and of the line parameters. The aim of this paper is to assess the effect of these losses through each of these two mechanisms. We show in particular, that for lines whose length does not exceed a certain 'critical' value, the surge propagation along the line is not appreciably affected by the ground finite conductivity, and therefore, it can be neglected in the computation process. Further, it has been shown that, for typical power lines, the wire impedance and the ground admittance, both frequency-dependent, can be neglected in the computations for typical power lines.

articleTitle: Electrically Conductive Metal Silicides for EMI/RFI Shielding
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Conductive metal mesh coatings on external surfaces of infrared (IR) windows reduce the electromagnetic and radio frequency interference (EMI/RFI) but are mechanically soft and easily damaged. Surface-doped semiconductors, such as gallium arsenide, have optical absorption and emission problems, while semiconducting carbide coatings, such as germanium carbide, suffer performance loss at the low end of the required temperature range. Electrically conductive metal silicides were investigated for use in erosion-resistant EMI/RFI protective coatings for IR windows and radomes. Selected materials were sputtered on zinc sulfide substrates, electrical properties were evaluated, and shielding effectiveness was measured.

articleTitle: Shielding of a Coil by a Ferromagnetic Disc
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A rotation-symmetric system consists of a conducting ferromagnetic disc and an exciting coil which leads a low-frequency alternating current. For the calculation of the disc's shielding properties we solve its eddy current problem by the help of two coupled boundary integral equations written for the vector potential. The integrals are evaluated by applying the Gaussian method, and by using polynomials of high order for the approximation of the unknown functions at the disc's surface. In the case of a non- conductive disc the problem can be described by a single integral equation of second kind. The kernels of the coupled integral equations are presented in analytical as well as in numerical form. As results we publish diagrams displaying the dependency of the shielding effectiveness on the disc's diameter, thickness, conductivity and permeability.

articleTitle: Measuring Methods and Measuring Setups for the Characterisation of Shielding Materials under Different Conditions
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The characterisation of shielding materials under different measuring conditions is still a difficult topic. In this paper, some measuring methods will be discussed, which allows the characterisation of shielding materials under different conditions. In a first part, the basic concept of both TEM-t and H-t cells will be discussed. The TEM-t cell has been designed for the characterisation for plane wave conditions, and the H-t cells is usable for the magnetic field, near field condition. Concerning the samples to be used, both cells are compatible and easy to use, without any specific preparation of the samples. Due to their design, orientation and field-polarisation depending characteristics can be studied. This property is a big advantage when studying gaskets and joints. In a second part, the typical electromagnetic behaviour of shielding will be treated under both plane wave and near field magnetic conditions, showing the different parameters which are dominant under each field condition. Some examples will be discussed.

articleTitle: Optimum Design of Nonuniform Transmission Lines to Control the Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An optimization approach is formulated in order to find the layout of a nonuniform transmission line system which presents a controlled radiation pattern. The control on the radiated field is performed on the basis of the comparison between the radiation pattern associated to the system layout with a specified reference radiation pattern satisfying fixed conditions. The radiated electromagnetic field is analyzed by NEC code and the global optimization techniques Simulated Annealing is applied to solve the optimization problem. In order to assure signal integrity, a penalty function related to the voltage transfer function is used.

articleTitle: A Compact, Broadband Electrical Field Probe for EMC Test and Measurement Applications
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A compact electrical field probe for EMC applications is presented. Due to the compact test set, the sensor must be arranged relatively close to the evaluation unit. This results in a significant influence on the probe caused by the interference from the housing of the evaluation unit. It is possible to a large extent to equalize the significant frequency response of the compact device through the use of optimized compensation techniques. Therefore, the E-field probes with small dimensions have a relatively flat frequency response between 100 kHz and 3 GHz. They also offer an extremely wide dynamic range which covers all of the relevant personal safety limits between 1 V/m and 1000 V/m.

articleTitle: Lightning Induced Voltage Calculation in Lossy Transmission Lines using the EMTP
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the implementation of the Rusck's theory of lightning induced voltages on transmission lines in the Electromagnetic Transients Program (EMTP). After summarizing the theory, the paper presents aspects of the implementation such as interfacing problems between Rusck's model and the EMTP. The paper presents comparisons between the proposed methodology and Nucci's methodology and also presents a study on the influence of losses in transmission lines using, as an example, waveforms of actual measured induced voltages in a distribution line.

articleTitle: Numerical Calculation of the Current Distribution on PCBs by Use of a Nearfield Scanning Method
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method for measuring the currents on a printed circuit board (PCB) has been developed. The magnetic field strength above the board is scanned by small probes. This information can be used to calculate the current distribution on the printed circuit board. The numerical backtransformation is based on the Method of Moments and uses Sommerfield's theory for stratified media to represent the substrate of the printed circuit board and the ground plane if needed. This inverse problem is inherently ill-posed and leads to an ill-conditioned system of linear equations which is solved by the conjugate gradient method.

articleTitle: Structure Compensation for Reduction of the Interline Crosstalk on High-Speed, High-Density PCB
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The structure compensation for the essential crosstalk reduction between closely spaced interline on high-speed, high-density PCB with finite copper thickness is studied in this paper. The analysis is based on the difference in the odd-mode and even-mode propagation speeds of coupled lines. The structure compensation can effectively reduce the crosstalk through proper choice of the structure parameters. For prevention of crosstalk between closely spaced interline on high-speed, high-density digital circuit, the ratio for line spacing against linewidth is suggested depends on substrate thickness and line spacing instead of using the commonly used rule-of-thumb of two-to-one directly. The practical considerations for the reduction of crosstalk energy by structure compensation for the coupled interline are demonstrated and discussed.

articleTitle: Numerical Computation of Transient Electromagnetic Field Radiated by a Power Transmission Line
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the authors suggest exact analytic formulations which allow numerical characterisation of the transient electromagnetic environment, during operation of circuit breakers or disconnectors, of a power transmission line. The proposed method is original because it takes variation with frequency of line parameters into account together with its series active losses. The method which is thus established with practically no simplifying hypotheses. Finally, its numerical performance (precision and cpu time) is better than that of previous methods.

articleTitle: Human Exposure to Electromagnetic Fields Produced by Personal Mobile Telephones
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The knowledge of the electromagnetic source and of the complex dielectric permittivity distributions of a model of human head does not allow the exact evaluation of the field strength and of the power deposition inside a particular human head, as a consequence of the differences between the model considered and the actual head. The problem is even worse considering that each man has a different head configuration. In order to point out this difficulty we consider some simple models of the human head and, by modifying some dielectric or geometric parameters, we show that the computed electromagnetic field can have big variations. On the basis of these results, we suggest an alternative way to predict the internal field, i.e., the use of a microwave-imaging technique. In particular, a probabilistic approach to the solution of the complete nonlinear formulation of the related inverse scattering problem is considered.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Behavior of Amplifiers with Active Feedback
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the Volterra nonlinear transfer functions of an amplifier with active feedback are obtained. A structural method for nonlinear analysis is employed in order to obtain these transfer functions and the optimum conditions under which the amplifier exhibits maximum linearity, and hence, maximum immunity to interfering signals. Simulated results performed over a practical amplifier configuration with active feedback demonstrate the validity of the maximum linearity conditions.

articleTitle: Simulation of Transient Protector Co-Ordination in a Low Voltage Power Installation Network using ATP-EMTP
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The ATP-EMTP program was used to simulate the dynamic transient characteristics of cascade protection circuits for a low voltage power installation network. The skin effect of the installation cables, the dynamic characteristics of the gas discharge protector and the varistors were considered. A good agreement was obtained between the experimental and the simulated results which shows that ATP-EMTP is an excellent tool for simulation of complex surge protection circuits.

articleTitle: Using Reinforcement Learning Methods for Effective EMC-Immunity Testing of Computerized Equipment
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the major problems in immunity testing of computerized equipment against electrical transients is their time-variant susceptibility. Since complete immunity testing of an operational cycle with hundreds of susceptible time windows is prohibitive this paper aims at providing methods for affordable estimation of mean and maximum malfunction probability in an operational cycle. For the latter reinforcement learning algorithms are used which automatically restrict testing to most susceptible time windows. This allows effective immunity testing also for safety-related equipment and supports effective redesign.

articleTitle: A Small Sensor to Measure the Electric Field in and on the Surface of Biological Materials in the Frequency Range 450MHz - 1GHz
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper a sensor is presented, which is able to measure the electric field strength in the frequency range 300MHz-lGHz. It will be easily possible to increase the frequency range up to 3 GHz. Two sensors with different sizes were realized, the total dipole lenghts are 1.5cm and 0.6cm. The sensors are insulated with a lossless material in the way, that the field response is almost independent of the surrounding medium. This is specially interesting for measurements in dielectric materials like simulated biological tissues. The sensors consist of a metallic dipole with a diode as charge. The signal is transmitted by high-resistive transmission lines, which show a very low disturbing influence on the existing electromagnetic field. The sensors are able to detect electric fields down to less than lV/m respectively 3V/m. The dynamic range is at least 40dB and depends on the chosen diode.
