articleTitle: Low EMI Susceptibility is an Acceptable Demand for Low Supply Voltage CMOS Integrated Operational Amplifiers?
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work we analyze the effects of electromagnetic-induced interferences conveyed at the input of low-voltage CMOS operational amplifiers. It is shown through simulations that a careful circuit design, which takes into account parasitics extracted from layout, can lead to opamp with a correct behaviour even in presence of large interfering signals conveyed to the inputs.

articleTitle: 2nd Order Interference in TV Receivers
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: TV reception in band III (174 ÷ 230 MHz) may be disturbed by the signals of radio station from the VHF band II (87.5 ÷ 108 MHz). The main reason for that is the second order intermodulation caused by nonlinearity of the TV receivers' input stages. The paper deals with the problem.

articleTitle: Shielding Performance of Enclosures against near Field Sources
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A Finite Element-based method to evaluate shielding of metallic enclosures against near field sources is presented. The method relies on the introduction of new boundary conditions on the internal surfaces of the enclosure removing the enclosure itself. These new boundary conditions are expressed in terms of equivalent near field source distributions and of equivalent wave impedance (admittance) distributions along the removed edges in analogy with Thévenin (Norton) approach in circuit theory. Also the presence of apertures is accounted for by imposing adequate boundary conditions.

articleTitle: AC-Characteristics of MO-Arresters under Pulse-Stress
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The influence of a varistor’s temperature on its leakage current is investigated for different samples. A method for calculating the ohmic component of a leakage current is presented. The dependency of the ohmic component of leakage current on temperature is compared to the dependency of leakage power on temperature. Leakage power is used as a criterion for degradation in the tests required by IEC 99-4 and ANSI/IEEE 62.11. The influence of pulse-stress on the AC-characteristics is investigated too. Several disks were prestressed in preceeding experiments. 400 pulse-currents of different amplitudes ranging from nominal pulse current (440A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) down to 55A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> were applied. The changes in the leakage currents which are caused by degradation are very simular to those caused by an increased temperature: the ohmic component of AC-current increases. This effect can hardly be seen at normal service temperature (20°C.. .40°C). But calculating the FFT of the leakage current, the effect of degradation can be detected in the third harmonic. An on-line measuring system based on the FFT is presented.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling of the Impact of an Overhead Transmission Line Overcrossing Structures on the Ground
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The space surrounding high voltage overhead lines is the area of major electromagnetic field action, its components (electric and magnetic) causing particular effects in objects and living structures (human beings included) neighbouring it. Charge simulation method is used to describe the electric field state around a complex geometry arrangement. The numerical results are processed with a graphic display software package and images are obtained which lead to straightforward conclusions.

articleTitle: Enhancements to the Land Mobile EMC Programs of the Canadian Spectrum Management System
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes some specific enhancements to the Land Mobile Electromagnetic Compatibility programs of the Canadian Spectrum Management System. These enhancements are aimed at improving the ability of these programs to handle interference analyses between digital and analogue radio stations, and to handle interference analyses for wideband channels (≤ 200 kHz) operating at or below 960 MHz. The intermodulation and harmonic analyses capabilities of these programs have also been extended.

articleTitle: Checking Compliance of Occupational and Residential Exposure to 50 Hz Electric and Magnetic Fields with European Standards
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper, after a brief analysis of international recommendations and of existing or proposed European standards for the protection of people from possible adverse effects of power-frequency electric and magnetic fields, presents the main results of a survey so far carried out by ENEL and aimed at estimating the exposure levels of ELF electromagnetic fields that might be encountered near the installations of generation, transmission and distribution systems, as well as in the vicinity of a number of electrical appliances. Data concerning the characterisation of various domestic, public and occupational environments, sources and activities (including exposure conditions associated with the operating methods for live-line maintenance of transmission lines), will be compared with the above mentioned standards.

articleTitle: Calibration of Electromagnetic Field Probes in Different Measurement Sites; Comparison of Results.
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In immunity tests small antennas (probes) are necessary to measure the strength of the ElectroMagnetic (EM) field radiating the Equipment Under Test (EUT). The calibration of EM field probes should be performed by a National metrological laboratory periodically (e.g. every two years). Nevertheless a test laboratory should have the capability of verifying EM field probes to ensure that the available probes are still calibrated. In this paper the calibration method, used in three sites (TEM cell, G-TEM cell and semianechoic chamber) available in the CSELT laboratories, is described and an error budget is given in each case. Comparisons of the results obtained in the different sites are done. These comparisons allow to draw some conclusions about the achievable uncertainties and about the site to be chosen for probe calibration in the different frequency ranges.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Millimeter-Wave Band Radiolinks in Digital Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Results of the analysis of electromagnetic compatibility of atmosphere radiolinks in the millimeter wave band in the cellular network are given. Models of frequency plan of cellular covering with 120° and 60° cell sectorization and with narrow directed antennae of subscribers are proposed. Calculations of the level of cochannel and interchannel interference from base stations (BS) at the output of the intermediate frequency filter of the subscriber’s receiver depending upon the location of the subscriber, coefficient of filtration of the adjacent channel interference and characteristics of subscriber’s and BS antennae are presented.

articleTitle: The Moment/Finite Element Method: Possible Applications to the Solution of Electromagnetic Compatibility Problems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Many electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) problems can also be formulated as electromagnetic scattering problems. Thus, in this context, numerical scattering simulators are becoming more and more important. Among these numerical simulators, the hybrid Moment Method/Finite Element Method (MM/FEM) approach seems to have the best characteristics, being computationally very efficient. The aim of this paper is to evaluate the reliability of the MM/FEM approach when it is applied to the solution of typical EMC problems: to this end we present some preliminary and very simple test cases, which allow the demonstration of the good features of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Time Domain Solution for ESD Field Penetration through Array of Apertures into Metallic Enclosures
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents a time domain approach for the analysis of the coupling between an Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) current and the internal region of a shielded enclosure with a slot. The application of the equivalence principle allows us to obtain an integro-differential equation for the unknown distribution of the aperture electric field. The numerical solution is obtained by an iterative procedure developed by the Method of Moment (MOM) in time domain. The use of proper impulse responses for space and cavity regions make the model efficient from a computational point of view, without losing in accuracy. Theoretical results are validated by measurements.

articleTitle: Sar Evaluation for an Anatomically-Based Model of the Human Head Generated by Different Types of Cellular Phones
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An analysis of the SAR (Specific Absorption Rate) distribution is obtained into the human head radiated by different types of cellular phones. The geometry of the cellular phone is described by means of a pre-processing system, developed in house, that starting from a graphical representation obtained by means of a mechanical Computer Aided Design (CAD) tool, generates all necessary data for the electromagnetic elaboration with the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) technique. The human head is defined by means of a set of Magnetic Resonance (MR) images recognised by tissues and organs. The recognition process is performed with neural network techniques and is validated with the help of neurophysiologists. Results show the SAR distribution into the head due to different types of hand-held phones at 900.0 MHz, the evaluation of the SAR into the tissues/organs. The FDTD code has been validated experimentally.

articleTitle: The Effects of Cross Polar Coupling on 3M to 10M Open Area Test Site Measurement Transfer.
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EMC standards allow for measurements of radiated emissions on Open Area Test Sites (OATSs) with various Equipment Under Test (EUT) to measurement antenna distances. Some standards, including the European generic standard EN 55 022 allow measurements to be scaled from one measurement distance to another using a scaling factor of 20dB per decade in distance, which is the 1/r fall off of field with distance. For example, to predict the field at 10m distance from measurements made at 3m distance, 10.45dB is taken away from the measured value. The fact that an emissions test uses an antenna scanned in height means that this scaling factor can only be approximately true, but fundamental analysis of the polarization characteristics of both an EUT and the OATS on which it is measured reveals that the transferring of measurements from one type of OATS to another is further complicated. Measurements are presented which were taken on a good quality OATS. These show that the fall off of field with distance from a real EUT is only approximately l0dB when moving from 3m to 10m measurement distance. The results also show that the prediction of the field at a different measurement distance has a high uncertainty. In the case of a vertically polarized antenna, the prediction can only be made to about ± 5dB. With a horizontal antenna the prediction can be made to about ± 2.5dB.

articleTitle: Signal Ground/Earth and Power System Earthing Coordination
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The environment of both industrial and commercial buildings provides many sources of electrical noise. The increasing use of solid-state equipment, computer or microprocessor-based control and communication systems, introduces a number of specific concerns with respect to electrical noise control. In most facilities normal earthing or grounding serves as a power safety purpose as well as the signal reference, and as the path into which noise is dumped by such devices as surge protectors and filters commonly used with electronic equipment. This paper is developed to identify electronic equipment earthing methods to achieve both a suitable level of protection for personnel and equipment, and suitable electric noise immunity for signal references. The use of double wound transformer, isolation transformer, even if improves the system earthing, it does not aid conflict problems between filters and residual current protective device. Originating from this considerations, this paper analyses possible improvements that can be obtained by alternative schemes of earth connection of the secondary circuit of the isolation transformer. Results of tests show leading improvements achieved by the alternative solutions as: independence between filter sizing and residual current limitation; reduction of high frequency current noise on earthing cable; improvement of equipment and personnel safety on occurrence of both faults and human errors; reduction of stress on signal cable shield in case of fault.

articleTitle: Improving Channel Isolation of the Microwave Diplexers
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An approach for improving channel isolation of the microwave planar diplexers by modeling series LC resonant circuits in the shunt branches of constituent lowpass filter, using the stepped impedance resonators, is proposed in this paper. An exact design procedure for the three-stepped impedance resonators is presented. In addition, improved characteristic of the trial microwave SSS diplexer with the channels (0-4) and (4-8) GHz is given.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling of the Processes of High Altitude Nuclear Explosion MHD-EMP Formation and Propagation
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The report presents a numerical model to calculate the gasdynamic and ionization characteristics of disturbance region and the parameters of a high altitude nuclear burst MHD-EMP. To determine the gasdynamic and ionization characteristics at the phase of the explosion plasma scattering the one-dimensional multiliquid model in sector approximation has been applied. The late phase of the burst disturbance region development at the stage of convectional rise of the heated air and the explosion products is calculated within the limits of two- dimensional model on the base of Navier-Stokes' equations. Gasdynamic and ionization characteristics of disturbance region obtained according to these two models were used as initial data for the definition of MHD-EMP. Numerical model of MHD-EMP parameters calculation is based on the solution of two-dimensional diffusion-type equation for the vector potential. MHD-EMP parameters at the ground surface were estimated and compared to the experimental data.

articleTitle: Voltage Dips and Short Interruptions, EMC Compliance
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents the problems related to voltage dips and short interruptions in low voltage a.c. and d.c. networks: EMC requirements of the apparatus and systems are considered. The EMC requirements are examined: taking into account the response of equipment and systems subjected to the phenomenon, the immunity specifications. the available mitigation measures, the laboratory tests for the verification of the EMC compliance.

articleTitle: The use of Synthetic Anechoic Chambers in EMC Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The technique to synthesize anechoic chambers for EMC measurements is described. It is based upon the use of high resolution direction finding algorithms. Synthetic anechoic chambers can overcome the present difficulties of performing EMC Tests in Open Area Test Sites

articleTitle: Implementation of a Three Dimensional Computation for the Analysis of Microwave Monolithic Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A general three dimensional computational numerical code is developed to calculate the electromagnetic properties of three dimensional finite size Microwave Monolithic Integrated Circuits using a Method of Moments technique, based on integral equations and Green's function formulation. An orthogonal parallelepiped cell description geometry is adopted to define the three dimensional permitivity and conductivity distributions. Starting from a layered structure, an integral equation is derived written on the inhomogeneities embedded inside the layered structure and taken into account by the Green's function. The unknown electric fields inside the inhomogeneities defined by orthogonal parallelepiped cells are described in terms of superposition of plane waves, satisfying the corresponding wave equations. A sub-domain Galerkin technique is employed to determine the fields inside the cells, for an incident wave, carried on a lossy microstrip line driving the circuit under investigation. Using the same code, the scattering parameters of a general multiport circuit can be computed. Furthermore, parallel programming processing techniques can be employed, providing the computational power necessary to reduce to a significant degree the corresponding computational times.

articleTitle: An Experimental Method to Describe Railways Radio Electric Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper concerns a method able to describe electromagnetic environment linked with rolling-stock exploitation, in the radio-frequency domain. Statistical parameters correlated with frequency- domain acquisitions feed indications about electromagnetic fields as a function of time. Employing this method it has been possible to make a preliminary investigation on Italian Railways 3 kVdc rolling stock, and a group of results relative to train passages, pantograph emissions, driving cabs, passengers coaches and external emission from other systems are presented, trying to define some constituent elements of the electromagnetic map of this traction environment. The definition of an experimental method able to make a statistical characterization from an electromagnetic point of view of wide and time- depending systems represents the possible original contribution of this work in EMC area; this method is applicable not only in traction but in other similar systems too (motorways, electrical high voltage lines and substations, etc.).

articleTitle: Evaluation of Radiated Emissions from Printed Circuit Boards and Cables at Post-Layout Level
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Because it costs to solve ElectroMagnetic Compatibility (EMC) problems late in the development process, new methods have to predict radiated electromagnetic emissions at the design stage. In the case of complex Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) with attached cables, a tradeoff between accuracy and simulation time must be found for this evaluation. In this paper the Radiated Emissions (RE) of single boards with and without an attached cable are investigated. A feasibility study is proposed for the modelling of these emissions. The results are compared with some measurements for validation. Some ideas are given to improve the models and to introduce them into an EMC post-layout environment.

articleTitle: Comparison between EMC Measurements in Frequency and Time Domain
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The subject of the paper is the comparision between EMC measurements in frequency and time domain. In practice, a replacement or supplement of frequency domain measurements by faster measurements in time domain can save time and cost. To investigate the correllations between EMC measurements in frequency and time domain, it is useful to divide the field of EMC measuring techniques in two parts: non-standardized measurements and susceptibility tests according to national or international standards. Non standardized EMC-measurements means basic emission and susceptibility tests to get an information about the EMC performance of the test object. For this kind of susceptibility measurements, in most cases the wiring harness is responsible for the disturbance signal amplitudes coupled in to the electronic devices. Therefore several measurements with different wiring harnesses and electronic devices have been performed in frequency as well as in time domain. The correspondance between these two measurement principles is very good as long as non-linear components are not involved. In addition the influence of non-linear components has been investigated to compare the characteristics of both principles. Emission measurements in a TEM-cell can be performed by using modern digital sampling oscilloscopes. An estimation of possible measuring uncertainities ensures, that the electronic device conforms with the requirements of emission standards. For special susceptibility tests according to international standards, it is very difficult to reach exactly the same severity level by measurements in frequency and time domain. It is very difficult to define equivalent susceptibility tests because this equivalence depends on the EUT. Some examples for electronic devices which are tested whith the same severity level in frequency and time domain are presented. The definition of equivalent severity levels for complex electronic devices i.e. microprocessor systems is very difficult. Therefore in practice, a replacement of frequency domain measurements by time domain measurements with exactly the same severity level is often impossible.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Common Mode Currents in Three Phase Inverter-Fed Motor Drives
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to find effective solutions to EMI it is necessary to use proper mathematical models of sources and paths of interference. Specifically, the analysis of common mode conducted emissions in large inverter/motor drive systems starts from modeling common mode current paths. The present paper deals with the development of a suitable mathematical model of a three-phase inverter- fed motor drive to be used in evaluating the effects of different modulation techniques on common mode currents.

articleTitle: An Efficient Algorithm for the Treatment of Multiple Frequencies with the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In a method of moments computation, one must set up and solve linear systems at each frequency of interest. Since solving a system at a single frequency can be a very time-consuming process, performing moment method computations over wide frequency ranges can require vast amounts of CPU time. We present an efficient algorithm where the impedance matrix is factorized only once and then used as a preconditioner in the iterative solution of all further linear systems. Examples show that significant time savings can be obtained compared to treating each frequency individually with the method of moments.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Robust Adaptive Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: On the basis of a priori information about change limits of the desired signal parameters the synthesis problem of adaptive antenna array robust control algorithms is formulated as a problem of conditional optimization with constraints of inequality type. Globally converging algorithms are obtained with use of a duality principle. These algorithms ensure the values sufficiently close to potentially achievable signal/(interference+noise) output ratio ones under the presence of errors in setting of a desired signal arrival direction.

articleTitle: Effect of 450 mT Static Magnetic Field on the Infectious Activity of Herpes Simplex Virus to Vero Cells
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Effect of a 450 milli T static magnetic field (SMF) on the infectious activity of Herpes Simplex virus (HSV) was investigated by in vitro Tissue culture infectious dose (TCID) assay using Vero cell line. No effect was observed in viral activity when HSV received the 450 mT of SMF exposure prior to infection. However, a exiguous reduction of TCID<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</inf> was observed in infection experiment between unexposed HSV versus SMF exposure receiving Vero cells. Furthermore, the culture supernatant which obtained from SMF exposure receiving Vero cell culture gave an antiviral activity against HSV infection to no-SMF exposed Vero cells. From these findings, it was indicated that the SMF exposure might be induced some antiviral agent(s) in Vero cells.

articleTitle: Reduction of Conducted EMI in Power Converters using Decoupling Capacitors
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The influence of a decoupling capacitor on conducted EMI noise has been analyzed for an elementary chopper mounted on a PCB. Proper modeling of the PCB interconnects with the Partial Element Equivalent Ciruit (PEEC) method implemented on a special-purpose CAD tool leads to a SPICE-compatible equivalent circuit. This equivalent circuit can be combined with the converter components in order to perform realistic simulations. The influence of a decoupling capacitor on conducted EMI is obtained from these circuit simulations. The simulation results are compared to breadboard experiments.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Compatibility of Permanent Magnet Brushed DC Machines
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The existence of EMI from DC machines has been known for some time, but it is only recently, due to new European legislation [1], that this topic has gained greater importance. The authors have already made a study into the EMI produced by DC machines as part of a survey into the EMC of machines and drive systems [2,3,4]. It is now the intention to focus the work on the permanent magnet DC machine, as found in many domestic and automotive applications. The paper covers the generation of a high frequency model of the permanent magnet brushed DC machine. This model is verified experimentally using a network analyser and can then be used to simulate the effects of different design parameters on motors with regard to their emissions. Existing work in the field has tended to be below 200MHz [5.6], but with the European regulations covering the spectrum up to 1 GHz it is important that the work covers the full frequency range required by the regulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Power Absorbed in Human Eyes Exposed to Millimetre Waves
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work the interaction of a plane wave at microwave and millimetre wave frequencies with a human eye (open and close) has been studied. The analysis has been performed by using the FDTD technique, and by using an accurate model of the eye obtained from photograph images of the human head. The obtained results have been compared with the internationally accepted primary limits on the SAR.

articleTitle: Wideband Noise and Spectrum Engineering
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Wideband noise is more and more often found to be the dominant mechanism of interference in compatibility studies carried out between radiocommunication systems, in particular mobiles systems. In this paper, we will remind all definition and regulatory provisions applying to the wideband noise and the physical origins of such a phenomenon. Some results of measurements are presented. Examples of compatibility studies, including statistical approach, will enable to illustrate the spectrum engineering issues which have arisen in various bodies and the kind of analysis which have been performed in each case for solving these issues.

articleTitle: Effect of Static Magnetic Field on Bacterial Infection to HeLa Cells
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper shows the effect of a static magnetic field on the adhesion of pathogenic Escherichia coli(E.coli) to HeLa cells. The number of adhesive E.coli to HeLa cells was remarkably increased after they were incubated in 450mT static magnetic field. There was also the dose dependency on the intensity of static magnetic field. In order to analyze this phenomenon, the growth enhancement of E.coli caused by the static magnetic field exposure and the susceptibility of HeLa cells to the static magnetic filed were examined respectively. However, those changes were not observed in both experiments. These facts suggest that the adherent phenomenon of E.coli to HeLa cells was caused by some unknown actions that occurred at the contact between the cells and bacteria by the presence of the magnetic field rather than by direct biological effects of the magnetic field on the cells and bacteria.

articleTitle: Analysis of Two Coupled Grounding Systems: Linear Grounding System and Plate Ground Electrode
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The unknown current distribution (UCD), distribution of leakage current density (LCD), self and mutual impedances, and distribution of surface potential for two coupled grounding systems (Linear grounding system: L-GS, and Plate grounding system: P-GS) are presented in this paper. A mathematical model of linear antennas (applied to the L-GS analysis) and so-called method of equivalent electrodes (MEE, applied to the plate ground electrode modelling) are combined to solve this problem. The GSs are driven by separate ideal current generators of power frequency.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Behaviour of the High Voltage Transformers at Very Fast Transient Overvoltages
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This work is an application of the Boundary Element Method (BEM) to EMC problems. The purpose of the paper is to present a possibility to compute the behaviour of the high voltage transformers in the high frequency domain (MHz). The transformer model considered is an electrical transmission line system, whose parameters are to be determined with the help of the field computation.

articleTitle: New Perspective in Broad Band Sensors Calibration
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A GTEM cell characterization in the frequency range below 1 GHz is presented in order to investigate its capability in broad band sensors calibration. VSWR, Electric Field Uniformity, etc., are measured and their values compared to specifications. A compact broad band electric field sensor is used to assess consistency and repeatability of measurements and comparisons between field strength values evaluated by this sensor, independently calibrated by manufacturer, and GTEM data are displayed. The optimum position of the sensor inside the test volume is investigated. In order to optimize test time and repeatability an ad hoc software fit to drive all used instrumentation is implemented. Preliminary results of Electric Field Uniformity in the frequency range over 1 GHz are shown. Finally, critical evaluation of GTEM performances is presented and suggestions are given to improve its reliability.

articleTitle: EMI Modeling and Measurements for Power Drive Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Due to the fast improvement of the performances of semiconductor devices (in terms of switching frequency, tum-on/off time, etc.), power drive systems (PDS) create a large amplitude of electromagnetic interferences (EMI) over a wide range of frequencies. This paper analyzes the generation of radiated EMI inside PDS. An RF circuit model of a IGBT is proposed. The near-field radiated emissions are measured and investigated. This kind of radiation is important to characterize the eventual interferences of the power section on the control section.

articleTitle: On the Model Extraction of Microwave Transistor's and MMIC's Packages from Experimental Data
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of extracting from experimental data a CAD-oriented, wideband, circuit model of the multi-lead ceramic packages adopted for encapsulating high-performance microwave devices is addressed. After discussing the limits of currently employed approaches, a general framework for the computer-assisted and systematic - though indirect - model identification and verification is set up. By combining E.M.-based circuit-diakoptics with the use of appropriate custom-made "lead" and "package-style" passive test-devices, a three-step procedure was developed which permits the extraction of both extrinsic- and intrinsic-package model parameters in a reliable and accurate manner, as demonstrated by the experimental verification data presented, pertaining to the characterization and modeling of a standard 100mil square (non-flange) transistor ceramic package in a frequency range of over 20 GHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Penetration of an Incident Wave through Conducting Screens with Displaced Rectangular Apertures
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to solve various electromagnetic compatibility problems, such as the coupling of electromagnetic waves with non-visible obstacles, the electromagnetic penetration of an incident wave through two rectangular apertures of different dimensions eccentrically “cut” on two horizontal infinite perfectly conducting screens is analysed. An integral equation system is derived in terms of the unknown transverse electric field components on the rectangular apertures, which is solved using the Method of Moments. To this end, entire domain Galerkin technique is adopted, based on Chebyshev Polynomials type basis functions, multiplied by a convenient square root factor, which satisfies the edge conditions at the rectangular apertures. The diffracted electromagnetic field is determined at any observation point, while the excitation of guided waves between the two parallel screens is also taken into consideration.

articleTitle: Hazards of Touch Voltages Due to Lightning at SLC40/41, CCAS, USA
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Launch operations present potential hazardous situation for human beings if conductive objects are touched during lightning storms. This is not deemed a likely occurrence because most launch complexes have procedures that prohibit touching of any objects during those periods. However, after the construction of overhead lightning protection systems, new procedures are being written to relax some of the 'no touch' restrictions with some attendant risk. To assess this risk, this paper utilizes techniques developed in previous analyses, and applies them to obtain human body responses to touching objects in a launch complex during lightning storms.

articleTitle: Radiated EMI Reduction from Microcontroller Systems using Spread-Spectrum Modulation of the System Clock.
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Computer and microcontroller systems operate synchronously with a system clock determining the speed of operation. The requirement for sharp clock transitions and the desire to increase the clock frequency of such systems to give ever faster computational speeds leads to lower and lower harmonics of the system clock falling within the frequency span of the recent European Community (EC) electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) standards for radiated interference (30MHz to 1GHz). As more spectral energy is held within the lower order harmonics of a square wave signal, screening the equipment to prevent radiated emissions becomes increasingly more difficult. This paper presents a novel application of the standard communications system technique of frequency-hopping spread-spectrum (FHSS) modulation to the system clock of a microcontroller, in order to spread the spectral energy contained in the discrete harmonics of the clock signal across the whole frequency range, hence easing the screening requirements of the system with a view to passing the EC EMC standard tests.

articleTitle: EMC Modelling of the Ethernet Local Area Network
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article deals with the electrical modelling and simulation of the Ethernet Local Area Network (LAN). Accurate models for the driver, receiver and transmission medium are presented which can be used to study signal propagation and electrical design guidelines for various LAN configurations. This analysis is then extended to investigate non-standard configurations such as the inclusion of backplanes into the network. A set of criteria is applied to the simulated results in order to interpret the electrical signals in terms of the transmission protocol, and to determine whether the configuration will function correctly. The simulation procedure is extensively verified by measurement

articleTitle: Microwave Techniques Validation in Power Electronics Interconnections Modeling
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present a modelling of a Power Electronics structure using a microwave approach. First, the advantage of using microwave technics is underlined. In a second part, classical coupled microstrips model is tested on a very simple geometry, and finally, simulation results are compared to experimental waveforms concerning especially the prediction of power MOSFET overvoltage at turn-off.

articleTitle: Harmonics Generated by Line-Commutated Converters, Operating in Non-Ideal Conditions
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The supply current of line- commutated converters is non-sinusoidal, hence injecting harmonics in the system. Multiconverter systems are formed by associating six-pulse converters in series or in parallel Characteristic harmonics appear when ideal operating conditions are considered, such as equal firing and commutation angles, equal current contribution of each converter when the parallel operation is considered, and also equidistant firing pulses and balanced system network operation. Two non-ideal conditions will be considered in the paper: unequal current contribution of each converter in the parallel operation, and unequal commutation angles in the series operation. Non-characteristic harmonics will appear in these cases. These harmonics are different tirom the ratio PK± 1 (k= 1,2,3,...) where P is the converter pulse number. A fast former transform program has been used to obtain tire supply currente harmonic spectrum, operating in ideal and non-ideal conditions.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Lightning Protection System as a Screening Measure against LEMP
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Modem structures contain more and more electronic systems sensitive to lightning electromagnetic impulses (LEMP). In order to protect such systems against LEMP different measures are applied. Lightning protection system (LPS) consisting of air terminations and down conductors with earth terminations may be considered as a screening measure against LEMP. However, because of open-work configuration its efficiency is relatively low. In order to assess the screening efficiency against LEMP of different configurations of LPS, adequate calculations and experimental tests have been developed. Several models of LPS with internal detector of electromagnetic effects have been subjected to the investigations. These models as well as procedure and results of investigations with adequate conclusions on screening efficiency are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: On the Effects of RF Interferences on Bipolar Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Modified Gummel Poon Model introduced in a SPICE simulator can be used to predict the behaviour of linear integrated circuits to RF disturbances. In order to obtain the RF distribution among the active devices of the chip, an .AC analysis is performed. From that distribution, by using the MG PM for the devices more affected, it is possible to carry out a .OP analysis for evaluating the drift of the d.c operating points. Measurements and simulations were made on many ICs obtaining a good agreement.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigations of Multifrequent Narrow Band Emission in the Schumann Resonance Frequency Range
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The quasi-electrostatic emissions in the frequency range 3-100 Hz presented as a group of quasi-monochromatic oscillations with random frequencies and duration in the range from several seconds to several hundreds of seconds have been observed on the ground-based station near Magadan, Russia. The emission generation could be associated with manifestation of an unknown physical mechanism.

articleTitle: Surge Recordings that Make Sense: Shifting Focus from Voltage to Current Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper proposes to establish a program for characterizing surge events according to the capability of a surge event to deliver a surge current through the power system in end-user facilities. This characterization would replace the conventional and by now misleading monitoring of surge voltages. The new approach will use a current transducer including a silicon-avalanche diode with the lowest possible voltage to “attract” surges away from other surge-protective devices connected within the facility. The voltage signal from the current transducer will then be recorded using any power quality monitoring instrument available to the individual researchers, providing complete current waveform parameters.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Caused by A.C. Traction Systems on Telecommunication Systems: Laboratory and Field Tests
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An a.c. traction system can produce electromagnetic interference on the metallic structures that are close to the railway line. In order to have a reliable evaluation of the effects of induced voltages on a digital telecommunication trasmission system, Ferrovie dello Stato, Italferr, Sirti, Telecom Italia and CSELT have decided to carry out laboratory and field tests. The purpose of the paper is to collect information for the new CENELEC Standard on this field and to define a 50 Hz immunity test for telecommunication equipment. This paper presents the results of both laboratory tests where 50 Hz induction effects were simulated, and field tests, where an a.c. traction line 15 kV - 16 2/3 Hz was used as a source of interference. The traction and telecommunication systems are also described and the results of both laboratory and field tests are compared.

articleTitle: Investigation of Resonance Effects in GTEM-Cell 1750
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: GTEM-cells are used for testing electrical devices for EMC. They are getting more and more accepted by international standards. Most papers yet published describe the electromagnetic field only on limited surfaces within the recommended test volume. In this paper the electromagnetic field within the whole test volume of the GTEM-cell 1750 will be under consideration. The electric field will be both calculated and measured and the received data will be compared in order to find out whether cell-resonances could influence the field level versus frequency. The investigation is of practical interest as the accuracy of measurements in GTEM-cells might get worse due to resonances.

articleTitle: Exact Field-to-Transmission Line Coupling Equations for Lines of Finite Length
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we further validate a theory presented previously by the authors for evaluating currents induced by external electromagnetic fields on a finite-length horizontal wire above a perfectly conducting ground. Then, we present an approach to generalize the developed method to more complex terminal wire configurations (other than the simple case of an open line) which requires to take into account the interaction between wire sections with different directions. The feasibility of the proposed method, in which the integral equation is to be solved only over a reduced region at the two extremities of the line, is demonstrated. The size of the reduced region being independent of the line length, the method is very efficient when considering very long lines.

articleTitle: The Magnetic Field from Twisted Three-Phase Arrangements
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The low-frequency magnetic field in the vicinity of twisted three-conductor arrangements carrying symmetric three-phase alternating current is studied by analytical, numerical and experimental methods. Exact formulas for the three cylindric- coordinate field-vector components are presented as functions of current, distance, pitch and conductor spacing are given and new approximate expressions are derived. Comparison is made with experiments.

articleTitle: Optimization of Magnetostatic Shield's Shape by Lagrange Method
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents new equations and boundary conditions on Lagrange multipliers that should be found when the optimal shape and structure of the magnetostatic shield is being designed. The algorithm of shield's shape optimization is derived. Also the equations related to Lagrange multipliers are considered when the objective functions of various kinds are accepted.

articleTitle: Optimal Phase Reflection Gratings and the Effect on Fields in a Mode Stirred Chamber
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method is introduced which uses phase reflection gratings on the walls of a reverberant screened room in order to increase the mode density. A measure, S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> , is described which predicts how well each grating succeeds in scattering energy. It is shown that there is a correlation between S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and mode density, and an optimal sequence has been found using the measure. The effect of a grating on the directions of the fields inside the chamber are investigated by examining the time domain response to an impulsive excitation. Experiments are described which compare three alternative methods; mode stirring, the use of a grating and the use of stirring together with a grating. It is shown that the grating used in conjunction with stirring is the best of these three methods.

articleTitle: Non-Linear Behaviour in Commonly Used Non-Polar Dielectrics at Microwave Frequencies
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In space RF communications payloads, it is increasingly required that high-power multi-channel transmitters and broadband receivers have shared, or closely adjacent RF feeds. Because of the large power level difference between the transmit and receive signals and the limitation of frequency allocation, intermodulation interference due to passive non-linearities in the high-power transmission path can be a serious problem. This paper describes work to determine the signal levels and dominant mechanisms associated with non-linear dielectric behaviour in this context. A novel measurement system for testing dielectric samples is described and measurement results are provided for commonly used microwave dielectrics.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference from High-Voltage Insulators : A Comparison of Hydrophobic and Hydrophilic Cases
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Small-scale investigations conducted in a laboratory have determined the EMI levels as a function of applied AC voltage for two types of ceramic insulators and three types of polymeric ones; in some cases, both new and service-aged samples were used. The results have been obtained for dry, simulated rain and simulated salt-fog conditions. Related larger-scale tests made using an outdoor facility under dry conditions have established the beneficial effect of employing stress grading rings on two types of polymeric insulators. The findings have been discussed from the viewpoints of the performance of the various insulating materials and the operational requirements plus service experience from the extensive usage of glass insulators and silicone rubber insulators on Eskom's transmission lines.

articleTitle: Electric Field Distribution and Soil Breakdown in Large Earthing Systems Subjected to Lightning Discharge
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Knowledge of the distribution of transient currents in large and complex earthing systems in power plants and substations subjected to lightning stroke is important for the power system EMC analysis. It is a common opinion that the soil ionization in case of lightning in large substation ground grids may be neglected. Consequently, all existing models for transient analysis of large substation ground grids neglect the soil ionization. This paper presents results of analysis in frequency and time domain that show high probability of the occurrence of the soil ionization in large area of the ground grids subjected to typical lighting strokes. Since soil ionization modifies the distribution of currents in the earthing system conductors, this phenomenon have to be taken into account in EMC studies.

articleTitle: Final-Test Results of a New Elevator Drive System with Active Filter Characteristics
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A modem Elevator Drive System (EDS) which fulfils the four-quadrant operation is equipped with two PWM inverters, one on the line side and the other on the machine side. It is designed normally to function at the input with a high power factor and a low voltage distortion. This paper introduces a new EDS with a control of the Line-side Voltage Source Inverter (LVSI) which enables the drive to work as an active filter. That means the total voltage distortion, caused by the drive itself and parallel operating loads at the Point of Coupling (PC) are reduced in compliance with DIN EN 61000-22 or DIN EN 61000 2-4. Practical results with a 28 kW drive demonstrate the effectiveness of the line-side control related to the Power-Factor Correction (PFC) and Harmonic-Power Correction (HPC), especially for the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> and 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonics. Additionally, the behaviour of the whole EDS has been simulated in our laboratory by an controlled dc drive as the load.

articleTitle: Lightning Electromagnetic Field Computation using the EMTP
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this work is to compute the electromagnetic field generated by lightning using the EMTP (Electromagnetic Transients Program). In this approach, the TL model is used to obtain the transient current distribution along the lightning channel using the EMTP ideal transmission line model. The electromagnetic field at ground level are computed using the dipole method. Good results were obtained. The advantages of this tecnique are the very simple process to compute the channel boundary conditions (current waveform for base current models, the cloud modeling, etc.) and transmission line parameters (corona, losses, wave propagation, etc.).

articleTitle: A Useful Simulation Tool for the Study of Electromagnetic Interaction in the Traction System
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with the analysis of the electromagnetic compatibility between the power apparatus and the communication system in traction applications. A new simulation program approach based on a dedicated software is presented. The basic structure of the program and the modelling approach utilised are described. The basic aspect of the new tool is the possibility of choosing the model for every single part independently: this approach allows for utilising different models for the same part without rewriting the simulation program. Some application examples are also presented.

articleTitle: Linear Antenna Structures Connected to Conducting Surfaces in the Combination of GTD and MOM
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The analysis of real or expected electromagnetic influences in the EMC needs powerful and problem fitting tools, i.e. calculation programs and methods.

articleTitle: Overvoltages in Telecommunications Equipment Grounding Wires Induced by Direct Lightning Strikes
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To clarify the advantages of a mesh-wiring grounding system for telecommunications equipment, experimental tests of direct lightning strikes were carried out using an actual reinforced two-story building. The current distribution in the pillars and girders, and the induced voltages in the grounding wires installed in the second-floor were measured, and the voltage differences between a single-wiring, a star-wiring, and a mesh-wiring grounding system were studied. The results were as follows: (a) The main inductor to the wires installed in the floor was the current in the girders around the wires. The induced voltages can be estimated approximately by applying a wire-frame model to the current in the girders. (b) The mesh-wiring system minimized the induced voltages between devices because in this wiring system all of the cross points are joined, minimizing the loop areas.

articleTitle: Calibration of Low Frequency Electric and Magnetic Field Probes
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the calibration of low frequency electric and magnetic field sensors. The most commonly used calibration arrangements and the typically origins of errors are discussed. For both the electric and the magnetic field calibration several practical problems, such as the influence of parasitic fields from other sources, power supply problems, the influence of objects close to the calibration systems and problems related to high electric and magnetic field values are dealt with.

articleTitle: Strategy to Reduce Electromagnetic Perturbations Conducted and Radiated by Inverters
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is shown that a sine-wave may be approximated by a sum of rectangles with lower steps than with PWM techniques, leading to lower THD and lower radiated field. Two control patterns are analyzed. Measured values of the magnetic field radiated by the transformers agree with theoretical estimations.

articleTitle: Investigation of Measuring Deviation and Field Distortion by Electromagnetic Field Sensors
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Within the scope of electromagnetic field measurements in any given inhomogeneous field distribution the experience has shown that several measuring errors occur, which depend on the geometry of the probe structure, the size compared to the wavelength but also on the field distortion of surrounding structures close to the probe. In a series of papers the structures of different sensor types were investigated and optimized. The investigations described in this contribution concern the measuring deviation due to field distortion. The simulation of different sensor types and their characteristics has shown which factors affect the deviation from the true field, and gives a chance for estimating the resulting error. This computation is done by a program for numerical field calculation based on the method of moments.

articleTitle: Differential-Mode Voltage to Common-Mode Current Conversion in Balanced Transmission System Interconnections
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Common-mode current is a major source of interference in balanced transmission systems. We propose a lumped-parameter model to analyze the conversion from differential-mode voltage to common-mode current. This model can be used to analyze the different common-mode current sources in balanced transmission system interconnections. Experimental results show that the conversion of differential voltage into common-mode current can be a major interference source.

articleTitle: Guiding and Radiation Characteristics of Planar Interconnecting Lines in Gridded Ground Structures
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A full-wave methodology, based on the Spectral Domain Approach (SDA), for analyzing interconnecting lines realized on gridded ground planar structures is presented. Their electromagnetic behavior is characterized by accounting for typical electrodynamic effects related to surface and volume wave excitation. In this contribution, both a circuital modeling methodology, based on the Z- matrix network representation, and the prediction of the radiated emission, obtained trough an asymptotic evaluation of the corresponding radiation integral, are derived. These methodologies are then applied to the characterization of a class of gridded ground interconnecting structures. Spurious effects due to ground current loops and to the finite size of the full/gridded ground are pointed out, and design guidelines are suggested.

articleTitle: First Remote Determination of Energy Release and Current in Intracloud Lightnings by Means of Radar and Electromagnetic Field Measurements
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper contains theoretical arguments and experimental data for a new method of remote determination of intracloud lightning currents and energy release for distances up to a hundred km by means of synchronous impulse radar and electromagnetic field pulses measurements.

articleTitle: The Transient Blocking Unit Theory and Practice for Protection of Sensitive Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A critical assessment of the effectiveness and the reliability of conventional shunt-connected protection systems leads to the specification of an alternative and greatly improved protection system. The new concept is based on a series blocking device (SBD) which disconnects the vulnerable load from an impinging transient and a shunt gas arrester (GA) which then diverts the damaging transient energy. The protection system formed by the combination of these two devices has been titled a Fundamental Protection Unit (FPU). This paper presents a detailed analysis of the FPU, assuming ideal characteristics of the integral SBD and GA. Then the paper presents a practical implementation of a TBU and demonstrates it’s performance as part of a FPU through a series of laboratory tests.

articleTitle: Voltage between Sheath and Cable Conductor Due to Conductive Effects on Underground Cable
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents an analytical - numerical solution for the voltages excited along buried cables by quasistationary conductive effects of complex earthing arrangements. It is assumed that the system considered is linear and that the earth is an isotropic, homogeneous medium of finite conductivity. The reaction of currents flowing in the underground cable on the potential excited in the earth by the earthing devices (primary potential) is disregarded. The transmission line model of the cable, a segmental approximation of the curve of the primary potential distribution along the cable and the concept of superposition have been used in the method. The method may be useful for evaluation of conductive effects on buried cables in many practical cases, which are connected with power supply systems, electric traction and cathodic protection as well. The technical application of the method presented is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: Models of a Cable Bunch Which Consists of Twisted Two-Wire Cables
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We investigate the magnetic field of a bunch of twisted cables which are statistically ordered with respect to their installation angles. The field of these cables can be calculated in a simple way with adequate accuracy if the bunch consists of a sufficient number of cables. As results of statistical investigations we express the total field by the field of a single cable which leads the overall current of the bunch. Furthermore the deviations occuring in the case that twisted cables are replaced by twist-free models are shown. For practical use we propose a specific model of the twisted cable which requires no integration. It is composed of twist-free elements, where the angles between their conductors and a referring axis depend on the element numbers. By reducing the element length the accuracy of this model can be adapted to any required value.

articleTitle: Magnetic Field and its Error Distribution Predicted by Inverse-Forward Analysis
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: If near magnetic fields measured around a metallic plane are given, by utilizing inverse analysis such as the maximum likelihood estimation(MLE), surface current distribution on the metallic plane can be estimated. Using this estimated surface current distribution, magnetic fields can be predicted by forward analysis directly. However, the estimated surface current usually contains the error due to measurement error and the coefficient matrix defined by the measurement grid and the surface scheme. Such estimation error distribution will yield the predicted error distribution when magnetic fields are predicted. A model source is set up and the magnetic fields around a specific plane of this model were measured. The surface current distribution and its estimation error distribution were calculated. Then the magnetic fields and its prediction errors at about 3.0m from the plane were calculated. The analyzed results of this experimental example showed that if the magnitudes of the measurement error are smaller than those of the maximum measured magnetic field by a factor of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, then the maximum magnitudes of the prediction error will be smaller than those of the predicted magnetic fields by a factor of 1/6. Therefore, if accurate magnetic fields at the designated distances are to be required, the prediction error has to be considered.

articleTitle: Sensivity of Humans to Low-Frequency Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have constructed an arrangement to expose humans to weak and well-defined VLF magnetic-field pulses (sferics) in order to search for corresponding alterations in the (Fourier-transformed) electroencephalogram (EEG) of both specially and randomly selected individuals. As stimulus we reproduced the magnetic field component of sferics which were previously recorded with high-precision VLF receiving stations, newly developed for the measurement of true waveforms in the range from 1 to 200 kHz. These pulses have a length of typically 0.5 ms and are naturally emitted during thunderstorms, especially by lightnings. The frequency of the damped pulses centres around 10 kHz and a typical peak intensity selected for the present study was 50 nT. Repetition of individual pulses was varied statistically in time intervals from 50 to 200 ms. A total of 48 persons have been exposed in the strictly controlled double-blind experiments. The EEG was recorded by standard techniques, utilising 6 electrodes and artefact controls, and a questionnaire was used to assess personality structures of the subjects. The present study was set up to check with an improved technique previous reports on alterations in EEG due to sferics exposure. In addition, we tried to investigate whether the presumed sensitivity to the relatively weak magnetic fields shows more pronounced person- dependent variations when test persons are selected in a non-random fashion. In order to enhance the chance for such an effect we selected 27 individuals who belong to particular groups in the population which claim unusual sensitivities, especially with respect to electromagnetic fields and weather-dependent complaints. As second group 21 persons were admitted, mainly University students, who did not claim particular sensitivities. Each test person was treated for 30 min whereby a computer-based random-number procedure arranged exposure or no exposure to artificially simulated sferics-signals in various successive time intervals. After elimination of artefacts in the EEG, time intervals of 4 s are Fourier-transformed and power values are computed for frequencies from 2 to 30 Hz. Comparison of powers obtained for exposed and unexposed periods reveals a certain trend to suppression of powers in the alpha band under field conditions; when the selected evaluation method is applied to all data obtained with one electrode (P3) (out of 6), a field influence is found with an error level of 6%. Thus, statistical significance of this first part of data analysis just misses the customary 5% level. The 'sensitive' subgroup revealed no trend to differ from the second subgroup. In a still continuing co-operation, an identical copy of our apparatus has been transferred to the University of Giessen, where similar experiments of the described kind have been performed with 52 subjects, mostly students. A significant decrease in alpha power has been found compared to the control group which was not exposed, partly with a confidence level of better than 5% [10].

articleTitle: A More Efficient Adapted Finite-Difference Method Applied to Modelling Crosstalk Problems between Printed Circuit Board Tracks
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the major areas of interest in the area of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) modelling is the modelling of electromagnetic coupling between printed circuit board (PCB) tracks. The non-homogeneity of many PCB geometries means that numerical methods must be used for the calculation of these coupling parameters. Conventional numerical methods for calculating electromagnetic coupling parameters are extremely demanding in terms of computation time. In this paper, an adapted version of the finite-difference method (EDM), a widely used numerical method, is proposed. Results obtained using the adapted FDM show good agreement with those obtained using the conventional FDM and other methods, while achieving the anticipated reduction in time with respect to the conventional FDM.

articleTitle: Theoretical Representation of the Electromagnetic Field Produced by Cloud Lightnings
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An analytical approach is proposed which allows the on-ground electromagnetic field produced by intracloud or intercloud lightning discharges to be calculated by closed forms. These could promptly be adopted in a number of EMC problems especially involving sensitive systems. The analysis throws light on some details affecting the field oscillograms. The discharging channel is predicted to taper down and to be virtually represented by an upright segment spanning the vertical projection of the realistic, often horizontally extended, discharge configuration.

articleTitle: Modeling of Some Non-Standard Coaxial Cables by the Charge Simulation Method
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple procedure based on the charge simulation method and quasistatic approach is applied to the analysis of non-standard coaxial lines. Results obtained by this procedure are verified by comparison with those obtained by available exact or approximate expressions.

articleTitle: Study of EMC Problems on Programmable Logic Controllers
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper after a briefly discussion on the effects of some voltage disturbances, as sags, interruptions, and swells, both on Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and on the entire industrial process under the control of the PLCs, summarizes the results of voltage sags and short interruptions investigations. They allow to characterize PLCs behavior in presence of voltage variations and to determine their sensitivity. In the latter part of the paper the most common remedies to voltage sags and short interruptions, adopted at customers level, are reported, and it is also described a compensating equipment, permitting to PLCs to handle voltage variations directly. In order to verify the suitability of the proposed solution the results of some numerical simulations are shown.

articleTitle: EMC and Broadcasting the RAI Experience
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The text gives a general overview of EMC (Electro Magnetic Compatibility) problems concerning Broadcasting with particular attention to NIR (Non Ionizing Radiation) protection aspects and related long-term experiences acquired in RAI.

articleTitle: EMC Analysis of Radiation and Immunity by Moment Method Utilizing Frequency Characteristic of Mutual Impedance
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The frequency characteristic of mutual impedance is found out by the expansion of the mutual impedance in a series in frequency or wave number. And the coefficients of this series can be obtained by sampling calculations of conventional moment method at several frequencies. By using this series, the mutual impedance is easily calculated with high accuracy. And as a result, the high speed spectrum analysis is possible in the moment method. Moreover this method is efficient in the time-domain immunity analysis using the transformed frequency- domain technique.

articleTitle: Calculation of Internal Inductance and AC Resistance for Finite Thickness Flat Conductors
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Microstrip and stripline structures are commonly used for signal transmission in high-speed digital circuits. The Multiconductor Transmission Line (MTL) equations provide an effective description of the propagation on these structures. The current distribution on the cross-section of the circuit conductors (usually of rectangular shape) is a function of frequency and any evaluation of the per-unit-length parameters in the MTL equations should take this variation into account. This work considers the numerical calculation of the per-unit-length resistance and internal inductance from dc to several hundreds of megahertz for rectangular conductors in the above structures. The problem is formulated in terms of an integro-differential equation for the total current density on the conductor cross section. The integro-differential equation is solved by the Method of Moments. All the coefficients of the complex set of algebraic equations are analytically evaluated by introducing the concept of geometrical mean distance. The proposed method is validated by comparing with the known values of resistance and internal inductance for various canonical structures

articleTitle: Interconnect Models for Commercial Simulators
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple procedure to include transient models of electrically-long multiconductor interconnects with low frequency-dependent losses in commercial simulators is proposed. The models are obtained by adding to the mode delays and characteristic admittances of the lossless MTL model a set of filters, with rational transfer functions, describing the distortion caused by losses. The filters are implemented by differential operators of relatively low order and the resulting models offer efficient transient simulations as well as improved numerical stability.

articleTitle: Measurement of Fast Voltage Transients Due to Gap Discharge in Distributed Constant System
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The measurement method of very fast voltage transients due to gap discharge using coupled transmission lines was examined to find the pure voltage rise curves. The measurement system consists of the distributed constant line system, because the voltage transients were very rapid. A characteristic of the gap electrode, which has a matched impedance for the distributed constant system, was investigated in the frequency range below 5 GHz. The voltage of power source in experiment was 510 V and 800 V because the Paschen's law holds stability in air condition. As a consequence of the experiment using this measurement system, the measurement method made it possible to observe the rise time of about 100 ps. It was confirmed that the measurement method enables to measure the high speed and high voltage rise curves out of contact with the main circuit. And so, the voltage rise times were varied in accordance with the voltage.

articleTitle: Calculating a Transient Electromagnetic Field Emitted by a Grounding System
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this study the author proposes a methodology for calculating the Transient Electromagnetic Field (TEF) radiated by a grounding system following a stroke of lightning. First of all, modelling of a grounding system based on localised elements taking into account ionization of the earth during run-off of very high current will be presented. The transient current underground and in conductors will be calculated by solving the nodal matrix equation. Knowing how current is distributed, the TEF can then be calculated using the Hertzian dipole method.

articleTitle: Introduction of Discontinuities (without Impedance Breakdown) Effects in a Transmission Line Method - Emission Problem
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Transmission line method allows to study the propagation of a pure TEM mode along the line, but they neglect radiation phenomena. These phenomena could be introduced in theoretical formalism in the case of discontinuities without impedance breakdown effects. This paper introduces an approach to include them in a time domain transmission line method. Comparisons with integral equations (full mode methods) results validate the method.

articleTitle: Feasibility of using FDTD to Model Fields from PCS in a Hospital Environment
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Proliferation of personal communication services (PCS), particularly such devices as cellular telephones, has raised concerns about possible electromagnetic interference (EMI) with medical devices including those used on the human body or implanted. While several methods can be used for computations of electromagnetic fields for EMI evaluation, the efficiency, flexibility and ability to account for the presence of the human body make the finite-difference time-domain technique a very attractive tool for addressing the problem. We apply this technique with several recently introduced improvements to model electromagnetic fields in the 900 MHz band in a typical hospital room with a patient on a bed and a cellular telephone model located at a distant and proximal (about 1 m from the patient) locations. We also model the electric and power dissipated for a person in the room and in free space, and compare the results. Maps of the induced electric fields around and on the patient’s body surface as well as inside the body are obtained. They are intended to be used for assessment of potential interference with critical medical devices.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analysis of Electromagnetic Monocycle Signals for Communication in Seawater
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of detecting an electromagnetic signal propagating in a medium with ohmic losses is investigated. The transmitted signal has the initial time variation of a Gaussian pulse. The effect of the medium losses is to distort the signal as it propagates through it. For a given signal and a given medium, the distortion is a function of the propagation distance. The received signal is the distorted version of the transmitted signal embedded in additive white Gaussian noise. We use a correlator receiver for the detection of the presence of the signal. If the signal is present, the receiver estimates the distance travelled by the signal.

articleTitle: A Simple Method for Analyzing the Shielding of Extremely Low Frequency Magnetic Fields by Shields of Finite Extent
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Imperfect shielding of extremely low frequency magnetic fields occurs because of magnetic fields penetrating through and leakage around the edges of shields which do not completely enclose the shielded region. The latter effect is the subject of this work. A simple analytic model for shielding by two dimensional perfect electric and perfect magnetic shields of finite width is presented. This model and a model for imperfect shields of infinite width can be used to study the relative importance of source orientation, shield extent and shield composition and thickness.

articleTitle: Impact of Ionizers on the High Frequency Content of the Radiated Field from a Lightning Attachment
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Scale model measurements have been performed to investigate the characteristics of lightning attachments directly to transmission lines and lightning attachments to transmission lines utilizing ionizer protection devices. It is shown that attachments to ionizers tend to produce pulse with higher peak current and greater high frequency content.

articleTitle: A Critique of the EMC Directive
publicationTitle: EMC'96 ROMA International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper discusses the EMC Directive 89/336/EEC in the light of experience gained in its application to date. This experience is analysed to indicate areas of possible improvement. A review of the purpose and salient features of the Directive is offered. Three broad areas of perceived deficiencies are then discussed. These are: • the general implementation of the Directive, especially its relationship to other European Directives, the way in which it has been interpreted in different member states, and how difficulties in interpretation are resolved; • the availability and applicability of standards, especially their deficiencies in satisfying the protection requirements, the way in which they are generated and revised, and the way in which they treat uncertainties arising from their use; • the use of the Technical Construction File route, with a discussion of the role of competent bodies and the problems of ensuring compatibility of approach between them. Particular illustrations of the issues are provided.
